6.1.1: Salutation to Śiva, who is together with Ambā, with his gaṇas and with his sons; to the lord of Pradhāna and Puruṣa, the cause of creation, sustenance and dissolution. ॥1॥
6.1.2: The sages said: We have heard the delightful Umā Saṃhitā, filled with many narratives. Now tell us the Kailāsa Saṃhitā, which increases understanding of the principle of Śiva. ॥2॥
6.1.3: Vyāsa said: Listen with delight, O children, to the Saṃhitā called Kailāsa. Out of affection I shall tell you this supreme, divine text, devoted to the principle of Śiva. ॥3॥
6.1.4: Formerly, sages of great vigour, performing austerities on a peak of the Himālaya, desiring to go to Vārāṇasī, came to a common resolve. ॥4॥
6.1.5: Setting out from that mountain and reaching Kāśī, composed in mind, thinking, We must bathe, they then beheld Maṇikarṇikā. ॥5॥
6.1.6: Having bathed there and duly satisfied the gods and others with libations, then having seen the Jāhnavī and bathed in it, those lords of sages went to Viśveśa, lord of the thirty gods, ॥6॥
6.1.7: bowed and then worshipped him, filled with supreme devotion; and having praised him with hymns such as the Śatarudriya, those masters of the Vedas ॥7॥
6.1.8: all regarded themselves thus: We have attained our goal. Through Śiva's favour their aims were fully accomplished, and they were ever devoted to Śiva-bhakti. ॥8॥
6.1.9: At that time, seeing Sūta, who had gone out wishing to see the Pañcakrośa region and had come back, they joyfully saluted him. ॥9॥
6.1.10: He too, having bowed to Viśveśvara, the god of gods himself, the lord of Umā, then entered the Mukti-maṇḍapa together with them. ॥10॥
6.1.11: Then all the sages honoured the great-souled Sūta, the best of Purāṇa-reciters, seated there, with arghya and other offerings. ॥11॥
6.1.12: Then Sūta, pleased at heart, looking at the sages of good vows, asked about their welfare; and they too told of their own welfare. ॥12॥
6.1.13: Those lords of sages, knowing him to be delighted at heart, spoke introductory words in order to understand the meaning of the Praṇava. ॥13॥
6.1.14: The sages said: O disciple of Vyāsa, most fortunate Sūta, best of Purāṇa-reciters, you are blessed, for you are a devotee of Śiva and an ocean of all knowledge. ॥14॥
6.1.15: The blessed Vyāsa, teacher of the whole world, consecrated you alone and appointed you to the teachership of the Purāṇas. ॥15॥
6.1.16: Therefore the Purāṇic lore abides in your heart; and all the Purāṇas indeed proclaim the meaning of the Veda. ॥16॥
6.1.17: The Vedas arose from the Praṇava; the meaning of the Praṇava is Maheśvara. Hence the abode of Maheśvara, his seat, is established in you. ॥17॥
6.1.18: Having drunk the nectar of the meaning of the Praṇava, charming with the honey flowing from your lotus-mouth, we shall become free of affliction. ॥18॥
6.1.19: Above all, you alone are our teacher, no other, O great-minded one. Out of supreme compassion, tell us the supreme nature of Maheśa. ॥19॥
6.1.20: Hearing these words of theirs, the wise Sūta, dear to Vyāsa, bowing to Gaṇeśa, to the six-faced one, to Maheśāna himself, to Maheśvarī, ॥20॥
6.1.21: to the god Nandīśa, son of Śilāda, husband of Suyaśā, to Sanatkumāra and to Vyāsa, having bowed, spoke this. ॥21॥
6.1.22: Sūta said: Excellent, excellent, O most fortunate sages whose sins are destroyed! A very firm resolve has arisen in you, one that is hard to attain for evildoers. ॥22॥
6.1.23: What was taught by the teacher Pārāśarya to the sages dwelling in the Naimiṣa forest, that I shall tell, O bulls among sages. ॥23॥
6.1.24: By merely hearing it, devotion to Śiva arises in men. Be attentive today and listen with supreme joy. ॥24॥
6.1.25: Formerly, in the Svārociṣa Manvantara, sages of firm vows were performing austerities in the Naimiṣa forest, frequented by all the Siddhas, ॥25॥
6.1.26: conducting a long sacrificial session, propitiating Rudra, the lord of sacrifice, and wishing to know his supreme nature and sovereignty. ॥26॥
6.1.27: They all dwelt there, longing for the sight of Vyāsa, ever devoted to Śiva-bhakti, wearing ash and rudrākṣa. ॥27॥
6.1.28: Perceiving their disposition, the blessed Bādarāyaṇa, the Self of all, the fruit of Parāśara's austerity, appeared. ॥28॥
6.1.29: Seeing him, all the sages, with delighted faces and eyes, served him with every courtesy, beginning with rising to receive him. ॥29॥
6.1.30: Having honoured him, they offered him an auspicious golden seat. Then, comfortably seated on that golden seat, the great sage Pārāśarya spoke in a deep voice. ॥30॥
6.1.31: Vyāsa said: Is all well with you? Tell me. In this great sacrifice, has the lord of the sacrifice been properly worshipped by you? ॥31॥
6.1.32: For what purpose has the Supreme Lord, Sāmba, who releases from saṃsāra, been well worshipped here by you in this sacrifice with devotion? ॥32॥
6.1.33: Your undertaking appears to me to be prompted by a desire to hear about the supreme nature of Maheśa, of Śiva, for the sake of liberation. ॥33॥
6.1.34: Thus addressed by Vyāsa, the lord of sages of immeasurable splendour, the sages dwelling in the Naimiṣa forest, of supreme vigour, ॥34॥
6.1.35: bowed to the great-souled great sage Pārāśarya, whose mind was delighted with love for Śiva, and spoke to him. ॥35॥
6.1.36: The sages said: O blessed one, tiger among sages, born of a portion of Nārāyaṇa himself, treasury of compassion, greatly wise, master of all knowledge, O lord. ॥36॥
6.1.37: For you yourself are the treasury of the graces of this Mahādeva, the sustainer of the whole world, the creator, who is with Ambā and his gaṇas. ॥37॥
6.1.38: With minds behaving like bees that taste the nectar of your lotus feet, we have become fulfilled this very day through the sight of your lotus feet. ॥38॥
6.1.39: The sight of your lotus feet, surely hard for sinners to obtain, has been obtained by us; therefore we are men of merit. ॥39॥
6.1.40: O greatly fortunate one, in this region called Naimiṣāraṇya, all of us, engaged in a long sacrificial session, are expounders of the meaning of the Praṇava (Om). ॥40॥
6.1.41: Having firmly resolved that the Supreme Lord is to be heard about, and reflecting among ourselves on the supreme nature of the great Lord, ॥41॥
6.1.42: we have not understood it at all. Therefore, O lord, you ought to cut away all those doubts of us, who are of little understanding. ॥42॥
6.1.43: For in the three worlds there is none other than you who can cut away this doubt. Therefore, us who are sinking in the shoreless, deep ocean of delusion, ॥43॥
6.1.44: rescue us by the boat of the knowledge of Śiva, O treasury of compassion. We are eager in faith to know the true meaning of genuine devotion to Śiva. ॥44॥
6.1.45: Thus entreated there by the sages who had mastered the Vedas, the great sage, father of Śuka, foremost among the knowers of the meaning of all the Vedas, meditated on the Praṇava, the entire essence of Vedānta, the Supreme Lord, ॥45॥
6.1.46: having meditated, in the centre of the lotus-pericarp of his heart, on Śiva together with Ambā, the liberator from saṃsāra, the great sage, his mind delighted, spoke. ॥46॥
6.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The dialogue of Vyāsa, Śaunaka and others, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
6.2.1: Vyāsa said: Well asked is this, O brahmins, by you, the most fortunate ones; for the knowledge of Śiva, which reveals the meaning of the Praṇava, is hard to obtain. ॥1॥
6.2.2: Only for those with whom the Lord, who bears the excellent trident as his weapon, is directly pleased, does the knowledge of Śiva that reveals the meaning of the Praṇava… ॥2॥
6.2.3: …arise—there is no doubt; not for others, those devoid of devotion to Śiva—so declares the Veda; this is the settled conclusion regarding the truth. ॥3॥
6.2.4: Through your long sacrificial session the Lord, husband of Ambikā, has been worshipped by you—this I have seen today and know for certain. ॥4॥
6.2.5: Therefore I shall tell you, O believers, an ancient and wonderful narrative in the form of a dialogue between Umā and Maheśa. ॥5॥
6.2.6: Long ago Satī, daughter of Dakṣa and mother of the whole world, having abandoned her body at her father's sacrifice on account of the reviling of Śiva… ॥6॥
6.2.7: …then by her own power that goddess became the daughter of the Himavat mountain; and on Nārada's instruction she performed austerities for the sake of Śiva. ॥7॥
6.2.8: On that best of mountains, when the Lord of gods had married her according to the rite of self-choice, Pārvatī attained happiness. ॥8॥
6.2.9: Then on one occasion the great goddess Gaurī, comfortably seated with her husband on the great mountain, spoke to the god. ॥9॥
6.2.10: Mahādevī said: O Lord, supreme ruler, performer of the five cosmic functions, all-knowing one, easily reached through devotion, whose form is the supreme nectar. ॥10॥
6.2.11: Having abandoned the body of Dākṣāyaṇī because of the reviling of you, I have now become, O Maheśāna, the daughter of the mountain Himavat. ॥11॥
6.2.12: Out of compassion, O supreme Lord, by the rite of mantra initiation make me permanently established in the truth of the pure Self, O Maheśvara. ॥12॥
6.2.13: Thus entreated by the goddess, the god adorned with the cool-rayed moon then replied to the goddess with a delighted heart. ॥13॥
6.2.14: Mahādeva said: Blessed are you, O sovereign of the god of gods, since such a resolve has arisen in you. Having gone to the peak of Kailāsa, I shall make you such as you desire. ॥14॥
6.2.15: Then, going from Himavat to Kailāsa, lord of mountains, he imparted in due order, by the rite of initiation, the mantras beginning with the Praṇava. ॥15॥
6.2.16: Having uttered those mantras and established the goddess in the pure Self, Mahādeva went together with the goddess to the garden of the gods. ॥16॥
6.2.17: Then, with those full-blown flowers born of the wish-fulfilling trees, gathered by the goddess's dear companions headed by Sumālinī,… ॥17॥
6.2.18: …Śaṅkara adorned the great goddess, set her on his lap, and remained with a joyful face, gazing at her countenance. ॥18॥
6.2.19: Then there arose loving conversations between Pārvatī and the supreme Lord, for the welfare of all worlds, directly in accord with the meaning of the Veda. ॥19॥
6.2.20: Then the mother of all the world, resting on her husband's lap and gazing at his face, said this, O ascetics. ॥20॥
6.2.21: Śrī Devī said: O god, the mantras you taught are held to be accompanied by the Praṇava. Among these, I wish first to hear the definitive meaning of the Praṇava. ॥21॥
6.2.22: How did the Praṇava arise? Why is it called Praṇava? How many measures (mātrās) are declared in it? Why is it called the beginning of the Veda? ॥22॥
6.2.23: How many deities are declared in it? How is the contemplation of the gods and the rest to be done? Of how many kinds are the actions declared? How is its pervaded-and-pervader relationship? ॥23॥
6.2.24: How do the five Brahmans reside in this mantra in their order? How many kalās are declared? How is it that it constitutes the manifest universe? ॥24॥
6.2.25: And how, O Śiva, are the seats of the relation between the denoted and the denoting? Who is to be known as the qualified aspirant here? What is declared to be the subject? ॥25॥
6.2.26: What relation is to be understood here? What is said to be the purpose? What is the nature of the worshipper? And what is the place and the mode of worship? ॥26॥
6.2.27: What is the nature of the object to be worshipped, and what is the fruit for the worshipper? What is the procedure of practice, and what is the place of worship, O Lord? ॥27॥
6.2.28: What is the maṇḍala in the worship, and what are the seer and the rest, O Hara? What is the procedure of nyāsa and japa, and what is the sequence of the rite of worship? ॥28॥
6.2.29: All this, O Maheśāna, explain in detail. I wish to hear it truly, if you have compassion for me. ॥29॥
6.2.30: Thus questioned by the goddess, the Lord adorned with the moon praised Maheśānī and began to speak. ॥30॥
6.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The description of the questions asked by the Goddess, in the dialogue of the Goddess and the God, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
6.3.1: Īśvara said: Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain what you are asking me. By merely hearing it, the individual soul would become Śiva himself. ॥1॥
6.3.2: Full knowledge of the meaning of the praṇava alone is the knowledge whose nature is me. That mantra called praṇava is the seed of all branches of knowledge. ॥2॥
6.3.3: It should be known as extremely subtle yet of vast meaning, like the seed of a banyan tree; it is the beginning of the Vedas, the essence of the Vedas, and especially my own form. ॥3॥
6.3.4: I, the God beyond the three guṇas, omniscient, maker of all, the Lord, the all-pervading Śiva, abide in the one-syllabled mantra Om. ॥4॥
6.3.5: Whatever thing exists, all of it—by the predominance of the guṇas, whether taken collectively or separately—they declare to be the meaning of the praṇava. ॥5॥
6.3.6: Therefore this single syllable, which is Brahman, accomplishes all aims. By it—uttering Om—Śiva first brings forth the entire world. ॥6॥
6.3.7: Śiva indeed is this praṇava, or the praṇava is held to be Śiva, since there is no absolute difference between the denoted and that which denotes it. ॥7॥
6.3.8: Therefore the wise brahmarṣis, regarding the denoted and the denoter as one, know me, the God, as the single syllable. ॥8॥
6.3.9: Hence the seeker of liberation, free from agitation, should know that very praṇava, the cause of all, as me, the attributeless Supreme Lord. ॥9॥
6.3.10: This very mantra, O Queen of the gods, the crest-jewel of all mantras, I shall bestow in Kāśī for the liberation of living beings. ॥10॥
6.3.11: In this matter, O Ambikā, I shall first explain the extraction of the praṇava, by merely knowing which supreme accomplishment arises. ॥11॥
6.3.12: One should first extract Nivṛtti, the letter A, and after that Indhana, U; afterwards one should extract Kāla, M, then Daṇḍa and Īśvara, the bindu and nāda. ॥12॥
6.3.13: Thus extracted, this praṇava has the form of five elements, consisting of the three mātrās, bindu and nāda; it ever grants liberation to those who repeat it. ॥13॥
6.3.14: Of all living beings, from Brahmā down to the immobile, this praṇava is truly the life-breath (prāṇa); therefore it is called praṇava. ॥14॥
6.3.15: One should place the first letter A, then U to the north, and M in the middle, and its end in nāda — thus Om. ॥15॥
6.3.16: In the Oṃkāra, O best of sages, place the first letter, which is like water, in the south, and likewise U in the north, and M, which is like fire, in the middle. ॥16॥
6.3.17: A, U and M — this triad in order — are called the three mātrās; beyond them is the half-mātrā. ॥17॥
6.3.18: The half-mātrā, O Maheśānī, has the nature of bindu and nāda; it truly cannot be described, and it is to be known directly only by the knowers. ॥18॥
6.3.19: The Vedas truly declare, O beloved, that the primal śrutis such as Īśānaḥ sarvavidyānām (the Lord of all knowledges) arise from me alone. ॥19॥
6.3.20: Therefore I alone am the beginning of the Vedas, and the praṇava is my denoter; because it denotes me, it too is called the beginning of the Vedas. ॥20॥
6.3.21: A is the great seed, rajas, the four-faced creator Brahmā; U is Prakṛti, the womb, sattva, the preserver Hari. ॥21॥
6.3.22: M is Puruṣa, the seed-bearer, tamas, the destroyer Hara; the bindu is declared to be the god Maheśvara, the power of concealment. ॥22॥
6.3.23: Nāda is said to be Sadāśiva, the bestower of grace on all; at the summit of nāda one should contemplate Śiva, higher than the highest. ॥23॥
6.3.24: He is omniscient, the doer of all, lord of all, stainless, imperishable, indescribable, the Supreme Brahman itself, beyond both being and non-being. ॥24॥
6.3.25: Among the letters beginning with A, each succeeding one is the pervader and the lower one is the pervaded; thus one should contemplate throughout. ॥25॥
6.3.26: The five Brahmans, from Sadyojāta up to Īśāna, abiding in the five elements beginning with A, are in order my forms. ॥26॥
6.3.27: O Śivā, eight kalās born of Sadyojāta are declared to be in A; in U, thirteen kalās having the form of Vāmadeva are described. ॥27॥
6.3.28: Eight kalās having the form of Aghora abide in M; in the bindu four kalās have arisen, belonging to Tatpuruṣa. ॥28॥
6.3.29: In nāda five kalās arising from Īśāna are declared. Through contemplating the sixfold oneness, the praṇava is said to have the nature of the manifest universe. ॥29॥
6.3.30: Mantra, yantra, deity, the manifest universe, the guru, and the disciple—hear, O beloved, the meaning of these six categories. ॥30॥
6.3.31: The mantra, as stated before, is the aggregate of the five letters. That same mantra becomes the yantra; I shall describe the arrangement of its maṇḍala. ॥31॥
6.3.32: The yantra is the form of the deity; the deity has the form of the universe; the guru is said to have the form of the universe; the disciple is held to be the body of the guru. ॥32॥
6.3.33: According to the śruti, which says that Om is all this and that all is Brahman, this very meaning is declared to be the relation of denoted and denoter. ॥33॥
6.3.34: The Ādhāra, the Maṇipūra, then after that the heart, then Viśuddhi and Ājñā, then Śakti and Śānti, in order— ॥34॥
6.3.35: —these are the stations, O Queen of the gods; beyond Śānti is that which is higher than the highest. He in whom firm dispassion arises becomes the qualified aspirant. ॥35॥
6.3.36: I am the subject-matter, O Goddess, through contemplation of the oneness of the individual soul and Brahman. The subject-matter has been properly stated; now hear the relation, O Queen of the gods. ॥36॥
6.3.37: Here the relation is declared to be that of denoted and denoter, between the oneness of the individual self with me and the praṇava. ॥37॥
6.3.38: The aspirant should be devoted to vows and the like, tranquil, austere, with senses subdued, endowed with purity and good conduct, a brahmin firmly grounded in the Veda, ॥38॥
6.3.39: being detached from sense-objects both of this world and the next, a true devotee of the gods and brahmins, and observing vows to Śiva, ॥39॥
6.3.40: having approached a preceptor, an ascetic who knows the true meaning of all scriptures, who has crossed to the far shore of Vedānta knowledge, the best among the wise, ॥40॥
6.3.41: The wise, excellent disciple, endowed with qualities such as tranquillity and possessed of good conduct, should diligently please the guru with full-length prostrations and the like. ॥41॥
6.3.42: He who is the guru is declared to be Śiva; he who is Śiva is held to be the guru — having firmly settled this in his mind, he should make known his own intention to the guru. ॥42॥
6.3.43: Having obtained permission from the guru, he should live for twelve days observing a vow of subsisting on milk, on the seashore, by a river, on a mountain, or in a temple of Śiva. ॥43॥
6.3.44: On the fifth day of the bright fortnight, or else on the eleventh, the wise one, having bathed in the morning, pure in self and having performed his daily rites, ॥44॥
6.3.45: having invited the guru according to rule and performed the Nāndī-śrāddha, and then having had a shave done, excluding the armpits and the private parts, ॥45॥
6.3.46: the shaving of hair, beard and nails, and having bathed with a restrained mind, then having eaten barley-meal, in the evening, having bathed and worshipped at the twilight (sandhyā), ॥46॥
6.3.47: having performed the evening Aupāsana fire-offering, the twice-born, accompanied by the guru, having given the fee prescribed in the scriptures to Śiva in the form of the guru, ॥47॥
6.3.48: having gathered the materials for the oblation according to the procedure stated in his own Sūtra, and having duly installed the fire according to its distinctions such as the ordinary (laukika) and others, ॥48॥
6.3.49: But one who has already established the sacred fires should properly perform the Prājāpatya iṣṭi in the established Śrauta Vaiśvānara fire, with all his possessions as the sacrificial fee. ॥49॥
6.3.50: Then, having placed the fire within himself, the Brāhmaṇa should go forth from home. Having cooked the caru oblation in that fire, with the distinctions of fuel-sticks, food and ghee, ॥50॥
6.3.51: the self-controlled one, having offered oblations with each verse of the Puruṣa Sūkta, and having offered the Sviṣṭakṛt oblation according to the procedure stated in his own Sūtra, ॥51॥
6.3.52: and having offered the concluding rites (uparitantra), the wise one should then sit on a seat, to the north of the fire, covered with cloth, deer-skin and kuśa grass, and, silent and firm of mind, should recite the Gāyatrī until the Brāhma-muhūrta. ॥52॥
6.3.53: Then, having bathed as before and then cooked the caru, the wise one should offer oblations beginning with the Puruṣa Sūkta and ending with the Virajā mantras. ॥53॥
6.3.54: This may be done according to the view of Vāmadeva, or according to the view of Śaunaka and others; of these, the Vāmadeva method is foremost, since that sage was endowed with knowledge even in the womb. ॥54॥
6.3.55: Then, having completed the remainder of the homa, he should offer the morning Aupāsana; then, having placed the fire within himself and worshipped at the morning twilight, ॥55॥
6.3.56: after the sun has risen, he should then in due order enter into the Sāvitrī; having renounced the three desires and uttering the Praiṣa, the formula of renunciation, in due order, ॥56॥
6.3.57: having abandoned the tuft and the sacred thread, and then having cast off the waist-string and the like, he should go forth facing east, or else facing the northern direction. ॥57॥
6.3.58: He should take the staff, loincloth and the like, as befits conduct in the world; but if he is dispassionate regarding considerations of worldly conduct, he need not take them. ॥58॥
6.3.59: Then, going near the guru, he should prostrate three times like a staff; then, rising, he should stand near the guru's feet. ॥59॥
6.3.60: Then the guru, taking the white ash produced from the Virajā fire, and having duly smeared that disciple with it, ॥60॥
6.3.61: should then have him bear the Tripuṇḍra, the three lines of ash, with the mantras beginning Agni; the disciple should meditate on me seated together with you in the lotus of the heart. ॥61॥
6.3.62: Placing his hand on the disciple's head, with a pleased mind, the guru should utter into his right ear, together with the seer and the other particulars, ॥62॥
6.3.63: the Praṇava three times; then that best of gurus should teach its meaning — the sixfold meaning, together with full understanding, ॥63॥
6.3.64: and in twelve forms. He the disciple, having bowed to the guru on the ground like a staff, should always remain dependent on him and should thoroughly study the Vedānta. ॥64॥
6.3.65: He should constantly meditate on me alone, the Supreme Self, within the pure and changeless self — the imperishable witness of Brahman. ॥65॥
6.3.66: The ascetic devoted to the disciplines such as tranquillity, who has crossed to the far shore of Vedāntic knowledge and is free from envy, is declared to be qualified for this. ॥66॥
6.3.67: He should contemplate the heart-lotus — stainless, sorrowless, clear and supreme, eight-petalled, rich with filaments, resplendent above its pericarp — ॥67॥
6.3.68: having contemplated it as the seat comprising all from the Ādhāra-śakti up to the end of the three tattvas, he should meditate on the subtle space (dahara) in its centre. ॥68॥
6.3.69: Uttering Om, the one-syllabled Brahman, he should, with mind ever intent, meditate on me together with you in the centre of that space. ॥69॥
6.3.70: For a worshipper of this kind there is attainment of my world, and, having obtained knowledge from me, the fruit of union (sāyujya) with me, O beloved. ॥70॥
6.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The description of the procedure of saṃnyāsa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
6.4.1: Īśvara said: Next I shall explain the daily rites of the renunciant, O Mahādevī, out of affection for you and in accordance with the tradition. ॥1॥
6.4.2: Rising at the Brāhma muhūrta, the ascetic should meditate on the Guru seated in the head, on the white thousand-petalled lotus. ॥2॥
6.4.3: The Guru resembling pure crystal, two-eyed, holding the gestures of boon and fearlessness, charming, bearing within himself the very true nature of Śiva. ॥3॥
6.4.4: Having worshipped him in due order with mentally offered sandal-paste and other items, and joining the palms in añjali, he should then bow to the Guru. ॥4॥
6.4.5: Whatever I do from morning until the end of evening, and from evening until morning, O Mahādeva, may that be your worship. ॥5॥
6.4.6: Having thus declared this to the Guru and then obtained the Guru's permission, seated, with breath restrained, self-controlled and with senses subdued, ॥6॥
6.4.7: he should contemplate the six cakras, from the Mūlādhāra up to the Brahmarandhra, supreme, full of all radiance, shining like ten million lightnings. ॥7॥
6.4.8: In their midst he should meditate on me, whose form is being-consciousness-bliss, the attributeless supreme Brahman, Sadāśiva, free from affliction. ॥8॥
6.4.9: The wise one, experiencing oneness with me, thinking, I am he, should then go out and walk far off as is comfortable. ॥9॥
6.4.10: The wise one, covering his head together with the nose with a cloth and placing grass on the ground, should relieve the body in the prescribed manner. ॥10॥
6.4.11: Rising, holding the genital, he should then go to a body of water; drawing water in the proper way, he should perform the purification diligently. ॥11॥
6.4.12: Having cleansed hands and feet and sipped water twice, remembering Om, facing north and silent, he should clean his teeth. ॥12॥
6.4.13: He should always do it with grass and leaves, except on the new-moon day and Ekādaśī; then he should cleanse the mouth with twelve mouthfuls of water. ॥13॥
6.4.14: Having sipped twice and cleansed the loins with earth and water, he should bathe with earth at the time of dawn. ॥14॥
6.4.15: Remembering the Guru and me, he should perform bathing, Sandhyā and the rest; for fear of prolixity it is not stated here and should be looked up elsewhere. ॥15॥
6.4.16: Forming the conch gesture, he should pour water on the head with the Praṇava, twelve times, or half that, or half of that. ॥16॥
6.4.17: Coming to the bank, washing the loincloth and sipping water twice, he should sprinkle with the Praṇava the cloth used for wiping the body. ॥17॥
6.4.18: Wiping the face first, then beginning from the head, he should wipe the whole body with that same cloth, standing in the presence of the Guru. ॥18॥
6.4.19: He should tie on, from the left, a clean loincloth with its string; then he should apply ash — its procedure is now told, O daughter of the mountain. ॥19॥
6.4.20: Having sipped twice and taken the ash with the Sadyojāta and other mantras, consecrating it with the mantras beginning Agniḥ, he should touch the body. ॥20॥
6.4.21: Then consecrating water with Āpo vā, he should sprinkle the ash with it, uttering Om āpo jyotiḥ and the mantra Mā nas toke. ॥21॥
6.4.22: Kneading it, he should make two portions, and divide one fivefold for the head, face, heart, private parts and feet, O Supreme Goddess, ॥22॥
6.4.23: with the five mantras in order, beginning with Īśāna and ending with Sadyojāta. Having smeared that portion, he should afterwards sprinkle with the Praṇava ॥23॥
6.4.24: the whole body. Then, washing the hands, he should take the other portion, knead it as before, and with it apply the tripuṇḍra marks, ॥24॥
6.4.25: with the Tryāyuṣa and Tryambaka mantras, the Praṇava and the Śiva mantra, on the head, the forehead, the chest and the shoulders, ॥25॥
6.4.26: on the navel, the arms, the joints and the back, in due order. Then, washing the hands and sipping water twice as prescribed, ॥26॥
6.4.27: the wise one, reciting the pañcīkaraṇa, should contemplate his own Guru, and perform six breath-controls in the manner to be described. ॥27॥
6.4.28: Taking water in the right hand and covering it with the left hand, he should consecrate it twelve times with the Praṇava. ॥28॥
6.4.29: Having thus sprinkled it on the head three times, he should then drink thrice, meditating with a collected mind on the Lord who is Oṃkāra, ॥29॥
6.4.30: stationed in the middle of the solar disc, supreme, full of all radiance, eight-armed, four-faced, wondrous, half-woman (Ardhanārī), ॥30॥
6.4.31: endowed with all wondrous qualities, adorned with all ornaments. Having meditated thus, he should then duly offer three arghyas. ॥31॥
6.4.32: Having recited the Praṇava one hundred and eight times, he should offer libations twelve times; sipping water again, he should duly perform three breath-controls. ॥32॥
6.4.33: He should come to the place of worship remembering Śiva in his mind; reaching the door and washing his feet, he should, silent, sip water twice. ॥33॥
6.4.34: He should enter there in due manner, right foot first; and inside the pavilion the wise one should construct the maṇḍala step by step. ॥34॥
6.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The description of the conduct of saṃnyāsa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
6.5.1: Īśvara said: Having duly examined the ground by its smell, colour, taste and so on, there, in a place pleasing to the mind, with a canopy spread overhead, ॥1॥
6.5.2: on the well-plastered surface of the ground, resembling the inside of a mirror, he should mark out a square measuring two cubits (aratni). ॥2॥
6.5.3: Taking a palm-leaf whose length and breadth equal that square, he should make on it thirteen equal divisions. ॥3॥
6.5.4: Placing that leaf there, standing facing west, and taking a very strong coloured cord at its eastern side, ॥4॥
6.5.5: he should stretch the cords east–west and south–north in all four directions, O Sovereign of the lord of gods; one hundred and sixty-nine ॥5॥
6.5.6: compartments then result. Its central compartment is the pericarp; the eight compartments outside it are here called the eight petals. ॥6॥
6.5.7: He should make all the petals white in colour, having made the pericarp yellow and the circle reddish. ॥7॥
6.5.8: Beginning from the right of the petal of Indra (the eastern petal), O Queen of the gods, he should colour the junctions of the petals red and black in sequence. ॥8॥
6.5.9: In the pericarp he should draw the yantra that reveals the meaning of the praṇava: having drawn the seat (pīṭha) below, and Śrīkaṇṭha above it, ॥9॥
6.5.10: above that Amareśa, and Mahākāla in the middle, and the staff (daṇḍa) placed on its head; then he should draw Īśvara. ॥10॥
6.5.11: He should colour the seat dark and Śrīkaṇṭha yellow; and those two, Amareśa and Mahākāla, red and black respectively. ॥11॥
6.5.12: The wise man should make the staff smoky grey and Īśvara white. Having thus drawn the yantra, he should encircle it in red with the Sadya mantra. ॥12॥
6.5.13: With the very nāda arising from it he should pierce Īśāna, O Īśvarī. Then he should take up the outer rows in order, beginning with the south-east. ॥13॥
6.5.14: These four compartments in the corner portions, O beautiful one, having filled with white, and the set of four next with red minerals, ॥14॥
6.5.15: having filled those four, he should fashion them as the doors. Then he should fill the pair on their two sides with yellow. ॥15॥
6.5.16: In the middle of the south-east compartment, within a yellowish square, he should draw an eight-petalled lotus, reddish, with a yellow pericarp. ॥16॥
6.5.17: With concentrated mind he should write in the middle the letter ha joined with bindu. Then in the south-west compartment of the lotus design he should draw a square, ॥17॥
6.5.18: and a red eight-petalled lotus with yellow filaments and pericarp. The third letter of the śa-group (sa), joined with the sixth vowel, ॥18॥
6.5.19: furnished with the fourteenth vowel and adorned with bindu and nāda — this excellent seed-syllable, O auspicious one, he should write in the middle of the lotus. ॥19॥
6.5.20: In the north-east compartment of the lotus design he should likewise draw a lotus; the third letter of the ka-group (ga), joined with the fifth vowel, ॥20॥
6.5.21: he should write in its middle, well adorned with bindu at its neck. In the three outer rows, all around in order beginning from the east, ॥21॥
6.5.22: he should take five compartments, O daughter of the king of mountains, O Śivā. In the middle he should make the pericarp yellow and the circle red. ॥22॥
6.5.23: The best knower of the rite should make the petals red in colour; outside the petals he should fill the gaps with black. ॥23॥
6.5.24: The four beginning with the south-east he should fill with white alone. In the east he should draw a black hexagon with six dots, ॥24॥
6.5.25: in the south a red triangle, then in the north a white half-moon, and in the west a yellow ॥25॥
6.5.26: square. In these, in order, he should write the four seed-syllables: having drawn in the east the bindu, white, and black in the south, ॥26॥
6.5.27: the letter u, red, in the north, then the letter ma in the west, and the letter a, yellow — having thus made the four letters, ॥27॥
6.5.28: and beginning in the row below the uppermost row, O beautiful one, he should colour the set of four: yellow, white, red and black; ॥28॥
6.5.29: below that the set of four: white, dark, yellow and red; and below, in the triangle, red, white and yellow, O fair-faced one. ॥29॥
6.5.30: Thus, beginning from the south, he should proceed up to the north (Soma's quarter), O Īśvarī. In the row outside it he should colour from the east up to the middle: ॥30॥
6.5.31: yellow, red, black, dark, white and yellow. Beginning with the south-east, O dear one: red, dark, white, ॥31॥
6.5.32: red, black and red — this group of six is declared. The sequence starting from the south is stated as extending up to the east, O Maheśānī; ॥32॥
6.5.33: that starting from the south-west is to be known as extending up to the south-east, O Īśvarī; and beginning from the west it is stated as extending up to the south; ॥33॥
6.5.34: that starting from the north-west is stated as extending up to the south-west, O Mahādevī; that starting from the north (Soma) is stated as extending up to the west, O Supreme Sovereign; ॥34॥
6.5.35: and that starting from the north-east is to be known as extending up to the north-west, O Ambikā. Thus the procedure of the maṇḍala has been told to you by me, O Pārvatī. ॥35॥
6.5.36: Having thus drawn the maṇḍala, the self-controlled ascetic should himself perform the worship of the Sun, for he is intent on that reality. ॥36॥
6.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The description of the rite of the maṇḍala for saṃnyāsa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
6.6.1: Īśvara said: Then, to the south of the maṇḍala, having spread a fine tiger skin, one should sprinkle it with pure water using the astra mantra. ॥1॥
6.6.2: First uttering the praṇava, one should next utter ādhāra; after that śakti-kamala, put in the dative ending and closing with namaḥ. ॥2॥
6.6.3: Having thus pronounced the mantra and seated himself on it facing north, he should restrain the breaths according to rule, preceded by uttering the praṇava. ॥3॥
6.6.4: Then he should apply ash with the mantras beginning agniḥ; bowing to the revered guru on his head, he should again draw a maṇḍala: ॥4॥
6.6.5: a triangle and circle, and on the outside a square, in order. Having worshipped it with Om, placing the conch together with its stand, he should worship it. ॥5॥
6.6.6: Filling it with pure, fragrant water with the praṇava, and worshipping it with sandal, flowers and the like, and with the praṇava seven times— ॥6॥
6.6.7: having consecrated it, he should then show over it the cow-gesture (dhenu-mudrā) and the conch-gesture; and with that water he should sprinkle, using the astra mantra, ॥7॥
6.6.8: himself and the articles of worship such as sandal and flowers. Having done three breath-controls, he should then perform the assignment of the seer and the rest. ॥8॥
6.6.9: Of this sacred Solar mantra the seer is Devabhāga; the metre is declared to be Gāyatrī; the god Sūrya, the Great Lord, ॥9॥
6.6.10: is the deity. He should assign the six limbs with the syllables beginning hrāṃ. Then he should sprinkle the lotus with the astra mantra, the lotus beyond the reach of fire. ॥10॥
6.6.11: On it the wise one should worship Prabhūtā and Vimalā, and then propitiate Sārā, in order beginning from the east and onward. ॥11॥
6.6.12: Then Kālāgnirudra, the Śakti named Ādhāra, Ananta, the Earth, and likewise the Jewel-island, ॥12॥
6.6.13: having visualized the grove of trees and then the jewelled house, and having worshipped the red seat, he should worship on its feet, beginning from the east, ॥13॥
6.6.14: the group of four: Dharma, Knowledge, Dispassion and Sovereignty; and he should worship Adharma and the rest in the corners beginning with the south-east (Agni's corner). ॥14॥
6.6.15: Then Māyā as the lower covering, and after that Vidyā as the upper covering; and having worshipped Sattva, Rajas and Tamas in due order, ॥15॥
6.6.16: he should worship in the directions beginning with the east and in the centre: Dīptā, Sūkṣmā, Jayā, Bhadrā, Vibhūti, Vimalā, Amoghā and Vaidyutā, ॥16॥
6.6.17: and the one named Sarvatomukhī; likewise the bulb and stalk, then its hollow, and after that the thorns, ॥17॥
6.6.18: the root, the coverings, the filaments of that lotus whose whole nature is radiance; the pericarp with five knots, and after that the petals, ॥18॥
6.6.19: the stamens, Brahmā and Viṣṇu, Rudra and the Self, the Inner Self too, and the Knowledge-Self and the Supreme Self— ॥19॥
6.6.20: having worshipped these, he should afterwards worship the yoga-seat called Saura. On the seat, the knower of the root mantra should visualize the deity's form with the root mantra. ॥20॥
6.6.21: Seated with breath restrained, by the root mantra alone raising the Śakti from his own root centre, by its power bringing it along the Piṅgalā path, ॥21॥
6.6.22: and having let it go out into the handful of flowers—then, in the heart-lotus of the shining one dwelling in the orb, whose body is red as vermilion, whose beloved forms his left half, ॥22॥
6.6.23: who holds a rosary, noose, khaṭvāṅga staff, skull, goad, lotus, conch and discus, who is four-faced, and adorned with eyes— ॥23॥
6.6.24: shining with twelve eyes—within his heart-lotus he should invoke him: first uttering the praṇava, then hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, ॥24॥
6.6.25: and after that, Mārtaṇḍa together with the Śakti of Radiance, I invoke, namaḥ—having thus invoked him, with the mudrā called Āvāhana, ॥25॥
6.6.26: mudrā, he should then display the mudrās of installation and the rest. Then, having assigned the limbs with the mantra ending in hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, ॥26॥
6.6.27: and having arranged the five offerings, he should worship three times with the root mantra. And on the filaments of the lotus, O Maheśvarī, the six limbs— ॥27॥
6.6.28: the wise one should worship around, in order, in the quarters of Agni, Īśa, Rakṣas and Vāyu. In the second enclosure the four forms are to be worshipped in order, ॥28॥
6.6.29: from the east up to the north, at the bases of the petals, O Pārvatī: Āditya, Bhāskara, Bhānu and Ravi, in succession. ॥29॥
6.6.30: Again, O beloved, Arka, Brahmā, Rudra and Viṣṇu are to be worshipped in the corners beginning with Īśāna, in the third enclosure. ॥30॥
6.6.31: He should worship these all around, in the middle of the petals beginning with the east: the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and the two Darknesses (Rāhu and Ketu). ॥31॥
6.6.32: Or else he should worship the twelve Ādityas in the second enclosure, and in the third enclosure he should worship the twelve zodiac signs. ॥32॥
6.6.33: And outside it, all around, the seven oceans and the Gaṅgās; the sages, gods, Gandharvas, serpents and the hosts of Apsarases, ॥33॥
6.6.34: the Grāmaṇīs, likewise the Yakṣas, the Yātudhānas, the horses made of the seven metres, and the Bālakhilyas—these he should worship. ॥34॥
6.6.35: Having thus worshipped the god Divākara with his three enclosures, he should afterwards, with collected mind, draw a square maṇḍala, ॥35॥
6.6.36: and placing on its stand a copper vessel wide enough to hold a prastha of water, filling it with pure water scented with flowers and the like, ॥36॥
6.6.37: and worshipping it with sandal, flowers and the like, kneeling on the ground, he should take up the arghya vessel and raise it up to between the eyebrows. ॥37॥
6.6.38: Then he should recite this Sāvitra mantra, which grants all accomplishments. Hear it, O Great Goddess; it ever bestows enjoyment and liberation. ॥38॥
6.6.39: Salutation be to you, vermilion-hued, of beautiful orb, adorned with diamond ornaments, with lotus-like eyes, holding a lotus, the cause of Brahmā, Indra and Nārāyaṇa. ॥39॥
6.6.40: Accepting this excellent arghya offered to you, with red powder, with golden water, rich with garlands and saffron, with kuśa grass and flowers, together with the golden vessel—O Lord, be gracious. ॥40॥
6.6.41: Having said this, and then having offered that arghya to Śiva in the form of the Sun, he should bow down, fully collected, reciting this mantra: ॥41॥
6.6.42: Salutation to you, Śiva, accompanied by Ambā, accompanied by your gaṇas, the first cause; to you who are Rudra, Viṣṇu and Brahmā, the threefold form. ॥42॥
6.6.43: Having said this and bowed, seated firmly on his own seat, having again performed the assignment of the ṛṣi and the rest, and having purified his hand with water, ॥43॥
6.6.44: and again having applied ash in the very manner described before, he should perform the whole set of nyāsas for the increase of the Śiva-state within himself. ॥44॥
6.6.45: Having worshipped the revered guru on the head with the five offerings, the wise one should then bow, uttering the praṇava, śrīguru in the dative, ending with namaḥ. ॥45॥
6.6.46: He should extract the seed-syllable of the five-natured letter joined with the bindu and with the fifth vowel; then that same letter with the bindu but without the fifth vowel; ॥46॥
6.6.47: then the lord-of-mantras letter joined with the fifth vowel and the bindu; having extracted these, he should then extract the saṃvartaka letter with the bindu. ॥47॥
6.6.48: With these seed-syllables thus extracted, in order, the wise one should bow to the guru and Gaṇapati on the two arms, and likewise on the pair of thighs ॥48॥
6.6.49: to Durgā and to Kṣetrapāla, standing with joined, cupped palms. Saying Om astrāya phaṭ, having purified the two hands six times in sequence, ॥49॥
6.6.50: having said apasarpantu (may they depart), then the praṇava, then saying astrāya phaṭ, with three strikes of the heel ॥50॥
6.6.51: having driven away the numerous obstacles on the ground, and with three hand-claps those present in the mid-air, and having cast a glance at those dwelling in the sky, ॥51॥
6.6.52: seated with breath restrained, remembering the haṃsa mantra, he should lead the living consciousness abiding in the heart upward through the brahma-nāḍī ॥52॥
6.6.53: into the clear great thousand-petalled lotus located at the dvādaśānta, to the Supreme Lord whose form is consciousness, abiding within the moon-disc of consciousness. ॥53॥
6.6.54: He should perform the drying, burning and flooding of the body in the order of exhalation (recaka) and the rest, with counts of sixteen, sixty-four and thirty-two, ॥54॥
6.6.55: using those seed-letters of air, fire and water, each with its own syllables beginning with the Vedic Om, in sequence. Having restrained the breaths, he should raise Kuṇḍalinī, seated at the root, as she goes to the brahmarandhra, ॥55॥
6.6.56: having brought her into the interior of the thousand-petalled lotus situated at the dvādaśānta, with the stream of supreme nectar arising from the moon-disc of consciousness ॥56॥
6.6.57: the body being thus drenched again, he, pure in body and rightly contemplating, then, saying so'ham (I am he), descending, places his own self in the heart-lotus, ॥57॥
6.6.58: and having made the self, nectar-like, enter into the Self by the flowing stream, he should here, concentrated, perform the installation of life (prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā) according to rule. ॥58॥
6.6.59: The yogī, with one-pointed mind, should contemplate that inner mātṛkā; then he should also place the mātṛkā externally, enclosed by the praṇava. ॥59॥
6.6.60: And again, with breath controlled, the wise one should perform the rites beginning with the gaze; remembering Śaṅkara in his mind, free of envy, he should perform the placing. ॥60॥
6.6.61: O Devī, the seer of the praṇava is Brahmā, its metre is declared to be Gāyatrī, and its deity here is I myself, the Supreme Self, Sadāśiva. ॥61॥
6.6.62: The letter A is declared to be the seed (bīja), the letter U is called the power (śakti), the letter M is said to be the pin (kīlaka); it is applied for the purpose of liberation. ॥62॥
6.6.63: Beginning from the two thumbs, he should wipe the hands down to the palms; then, O Queen of gods, saying Om, he should begin the hand-nyāsa. ॥63॥
6.6.64: Beginning with the thumb of the right hand, in due order, he should place the syllables up to the little finger of the left hand, in sequence as before. ॥64॥
6.6.65: Then, uttering A, U and M joined with the bindu, each ending with namaḥ, he should place them everywhere, beginning with the heart. ॥65॥
6.6.66: First extracting the letter A, he should then join the name Brahmātman in the dative, ending with namaḥ, and apply it to the heart; and likewise again: ॥66॥
6.6.67: he should place the letter U together with Viṣṇu on the region of the head, and the letter M together with Rudra on the topknot. ॥67॥
6.6.68: Having spoken thus, the sage who knows the mantras should place the kavaca and netra limb-mantras on the eyes and head, O Queen of the god of gods, with an attentive mind. ॥68॥
6.6.69: He should place the five Brahma-mantras according to the divisions of limbs, faces and kalās; he should place them on the head, face, heart, private parts and feet. ॥69॥
6.6.70: The five kalās of Īśāna are to be placed in order on these five places; then the kalās of Tatpuruṣa too, on the four faces, ॥70॥
6.6.71: the four are to be placed in order beginning with the east. On the heart, throat, shoulders, navel, belly, back and chest ॥71॥
6.6.72: the eight kalās of Aghora are to be worshipped in due order. Afterwards, the thirteen kalās, on the anus, penis, thighs, knees, ॥72॥
6.6.73: shanks, buttocks, hips and sides, he should contemplate as those of Vāmadeva. The eight kalās of Sadyojāta too, beginning on the eyes, in due order, ॥73॥
6.6.74: those kalās that have been declared, the best knower of ritual should thus arrange also on the two feet, the two hands, the nose, the head and the two arms. ॥74॥
6.6.75: Having thus completely performed the nyāsa of the thirty-eight kalās, the wise one who knows the praṇava should afterwards perform the praṇava-nyāsa: ॥75॥
6.6.76: on the two arms, on the elbows and likewise on the wrists, on the sides, belly and shanks, on the feet, and likewise on the back. ॥76॥
6.6.77: Having thus performed the placing of the praṇava, the one skilled in nyāsa should perform the haṃsa-nyāsa, O You who awaken one to the Supreme Self. ॥77॥
6.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The description of nyāsa, in the procedure of saṃnyāsa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
6.7.1: Īśvara said: On his own left he should prepare a square maṇḍala. Having worshipped it with Om, he should set in it a conch purified by the astra mantra, ॥1॥
6.7.2: having placed it together with its stand, he should then worship it with the praṇava, filling it with pure water made fragrant with sandal and the like. ॥2॥
6.7.3: Having worshipped it with fragrance, flowers and the rest, and having consecrated it seven times with the praṇava, he should then display over it the dhenu-mudrā ॥3॥
6.7.4: and the conch-mudrā. In front he should design a square, within it a half-moon, and within that a triangle, ॥4॥
6.7.5: then a hexagon and a circle — thus he should prepare this maṇḍala. Having worshipped it with fragrance, flowers and the rest with the praṇava, then in its centre ॥5॥
6.7.6: having placed the arghya vessel with its stand, he should worship it with fragrance and the rest. Having filled it with pure water, he should put into that vessel ॥6॥
6.7.7: tips of kuśa grass, unbroken rice grains, barley, paddy and sesame, ghee, white mustard and flowers, and sacred ash, O fair-faced one. ॥7॥
6.7.8: Having worshipped it with fragrance, flowers and the rest using the mantras beginning with Sadyojāta, the six limb-mantras and the praṇava, and having consecrated it with the armour (kavaca) mantra, ॥8॥
6.7.9: and having veiled it, he should display the astra gesture with the astra mantra for protection, and the dhenu-mudrā; with that same water he should sprinkle, using the astra mantra, ॥9॥
6.7.10: himself and also the articles of worship such as fragrance and flowers. On the petal of the lotus in the north-east (Īśāna) direction, preceded by uttering the praṇava, ॥10॥
6.7.11: he should set up a seat with gurvāsanāya namaḥ (salutation to the guru's seat), and there he should fashion the image of the guru as instructed. ॥11॥
6.7.12: Uttering the praṇava, guṃ, gurubhyaḥ and at the end namaḥ, and having invoked the preceptor, he should then meditate on him as seated facing south: ॥12॥
6.7.13: with a very serene face, gentle, spotless like pure crystal, with hands showing the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, two-eyed, the very embodiment of Śiva. ॥13॥
6.7.14: Having meditated thus, he should worship him in due order with fragrance, flowers and the rest. On the south-west petal of the lotus, upon the seat of Gaṇapati, ॥14॥
6.7.15: having fashioned the image right there and invoked him with the mantra gaṇānāṃ tvā, he should then meditate on the god with a one-pointed mind: ॥15॥
6.7.16: red in colour, of huge body, adorned with all ornaments, holding in his lotus-hands the noose, the goad, the rosary and the gesture granting desires, ॥16॥
6.7.17: the elephant-faced lord who destroys all the hosts of obstacles of the worshipper. Having meditated thus, he should worship with fragrance, flowers and other offerings, ॥17॥
6.7.18: and then, having offered food (naivedya) consisting of plantains, coconuts, mangoes, other fruits and laḍḍus, he should bow to the elephant-faced one. ॥18॥
6.7.19: On the north-west (Vāyu's) petal of the lotus, having conceived the seat of Skanda and fashioned Skanda's image, the wise one should invoke Skanda. ॥19॥
6.7.20: Having recited the Skanda-Gāyatrī, he should then meditate on Kumāra, resembling the rising sun, whose mount is the excellent peacock, ॥20॥
6.7.21: four-armed, of noble limbs, adorned with a crown and other ornaments, with hands in the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, holding the spear (śakti) and the cock. ॥21॥
6.7.22: Having thus meditated and then worshipped him in due order with fragrance and other offerings, he should worship the one stationed at the right door-post of the eastern gate, ॥22॥
6.7.23: Nandin himself, lord of the inner palace, he should properly worship — him who is like a mountain of gold, adorned with all ornaments, ॥23॥
6.7.24: crowned with the crescent moon, gentle, three-eyed and four-armed, the mighty one holding a blazing trident, a deer, a chisel-axe (ṭaṅka) and a golden staff, ॥24॥
6.7.25: with a face shining like the orb of the moon, or else monkey-faced. Likewise to his north he should worship his wife, the daughter of the Maruts, ॥25॥
6.7.26: Suyaśā, of good vows, devoted to adorning the feet of the Mother — having worshipped her duly with fragrance, flowers and other offerings, ॥26॥
6.7.27: he should then sprinkle the lotus with drops of the conch-water consecrated with the astra mantra, and afterwards arrange the seat, beginning with the Support (ādhāra), in proper order. ॥27॥
6.7.28: He should meditate below, on the ground, on the auspicious, dark Ādhāraśakti (Power of Support); in front of her, on Ananta with uplifted neck, coiled in form, ॥28॥
6.7.29: white, five-hooded, as though licking the sky; above him an auspicious seat with lions as its four legs. ॥29॥
6.7.30: Dharma, knowledge, dispassion and sovereignty are its legs, placed from the south-east onward, white, yellow, red and dark in colour respectively. ॥30॥
6.7.31: Adharma and the rest, from the east up to the north in order, he should visualize as its body-parts, resembling the rājāvarta gem (lapis lazuli). ॥31॥
6.7.32: Then, having visualized the lower and upper coverings, the bulb, the stalk and the thorns, the petals and so on, and the pericarp, he should worship them in order. ॥32॥
6.7.33: On the petals are the eight siddhis, and on the filaments the śaktis; the eight Rudras, Vāma and the rest, are placed all around in order beginning from the east. ॥33॥
6.7.34: On the pericarp is dispassion; on the seeds the nine śaktis, Vāmā and the rest, from the east onward, and at their end Manonmanī. ॥34॥
6.7.35: In the bulb is dharma, of the nature of Śiva; in the stalk knowledge resting on Śiva; above the pericarp the circles of fire, sun and moon, ॥35॥
6.7.36: and beyond that the triad of principles: ātman, vidyā and the one called Śiva. Above all the seats, a comfortable seat, brilliant with variegated flowers, ॥36॥
6.7.37: exceedingly radiant through the Vidyā called the space of the supreme ether — having arranged this seat for the image, preceded by the placing of flowers, ॥37॥
6.7.38: from the Ādhāraśakti up to the seat of Śuddhavidyā, each with its name-mantra beginning with Om, ending in the dative case and concluding with namaḥ — ॥38॥
6.7.39: having uttered these, the learned one should worship; this is the order of the rite everywhere. As before, distinguishing them by limbs, faces and kalās, the five Brahmans ॥39॥
6.7.40: he should place in order upon the image, skilled in their respective mudrās. Then, standing with joined palms holding flowers, he should invoke the god. ॥40॥
6.7.41: Reciting the mantra that begins with sadyojātaṃ prapadyāmi and ends with Om, and raising the sound (nāda) that rises from the ādhāra centre by piercing the twelve knots, ॥41॥
6.7.42: having uttered it up to the brahmarandhra, one should meditate on the God who is the object of the Oṃkāra, resembling pure crystal, partless and imperishable, ॥42॥
6.7.43: the cause of all the worlds, consisting of all the worlds, the Supreme, abiding within and without having pervaded all, smaller than the atom and greatest of all, ॥43॥
6.7.44: the imperishable Lord, seen without effort by devotees, yet beyond the reach even of gods such as Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu and Rudra, ॥44॥
6.7.45: the essence of the Vedas, declared in scripture to be beyond the reach of the learned, without beginning, middle or end, the medicine for those afflicted by the disease of worldly existence. ॥45॥
6.7.46: Having thus meditated on the Supreme Lord with a concentrated mind, one should perform invocation, installation, confinement, gazing, ॥46॥
6.7.47: and obeisance, forming the mudrās one by one. One should meditate on Sadāśiva, the God himself, who is both with parts and without parts: ॥47॥
6.7.48: resembling pure crystal, serene, of cool radiance, like a ring of lightning, adorned with a crown of matted locks, ॥48॥
6.7.49: clothed in a tiger skin, his lotus face gently smiling, his palms, soles and lips resembling red lotus petals, ॥49॥
6.7.50: endowed with all auspicious marks, adorned with all ornaments, his hands holding divine weapons, anointed with divine fragrances, ॥50॥
6.7.51: five-faced, ten-armed, with a digit of the moon as his crest-jewel. His eastern face is gentle, with a radiance like the rising sun, ॥51॥
6.7.52: rich with three lotus eyes, crested with the young moon. The southern face has a lovely radiance like a dark rain cloud, ॥52॥
6.7.53: crooked with frowning brows, terrible, with three red round eyes, fearsome with fangs, hard to behold, with quivering, sprout-like lips; ॥53॥
6.7.54: the northern face resembles coral, is adorned with dark curls, full of grace, three-eyed, crested with the half-moon; ॥54॥
6.7.55: the western face shines like the full moon, radiant with three eyes, bearing the crescent, gentle, charming with a soft smile; ॥55॥
6.7.56: the fifth face resembles crystal, shines brightly with the streak of the moon, is exceedingly gentle and radiant with three wide-open eyes. ॥56॥
6.7.57: On the right his hands shine with the trident, axe, thunderbolt, sword and fire; ॥57॥
6.7.58: on the left they shine with the Pināka bow, the iron arrow, the bell, the noose and the goad. He is pervaded by Nivṛtti kalā up to the knees, and by Pratiṣṭhā up to the navel, ॥58॥
6.7.59: likewise by Vidyā up to the throat, by Śāntā up to the forehead, and above that by the supreme kalā called Śāntyatītā. ॥59॥
6.7.60: Hence he is pervading the five paths (adhvans), his body made of the five kalās; the ancient God, with Īśāna as his crown and Tatpuruṣa as his face, ॥60॥
6.7.61: likewise the Great Lord with Aghora as his heart, Vāmadeva as his private part and Sadyojāta as his feet; his form consists of the thirty-eight kalās, ॥61॥
6.7.62: the Lord consisting of the mātṛkā letters, consisting of the five Brahman mantras, consisting of what is called the Oṃkāra, and consisting of the haṃsa-nyāsa, ॥62॥
6.7.63: the God consisting of the five-syllabled mantra and likewise of the six-syllabled, consisting of the six limbs (aṅgas) and endowed with the six jātis. ॥63॥
6.7.64: Having thus meditated, then one should invoke you, Manonmanī Gaurī, on my left side, with devotion, using the mantra gaurīr mimāya preceded by the praṇava; ॥64॥
6.7.65: having invoked you, O Īśvarī, one should perform the rites as before, up to the obeisance. Then, O Queen of gods, the sage with concentrated mind should meditate on you: ॥65॥
6.7.66: shining like the petal of a full-blown lotus, with wide, long eyes, a face like the full moon, and dark curly hair, ॥66॥
6.7.67: resembling a blue lotus petal, crested with the half-moon, with very round, firm, high, smooth and full breasts, ॥67॥
6.7.68: slender-waisted, broad-hipped, wearing a very fine yellow garment, endowed with all ornaments, bright with a tilaka mark on the forehead, ॥68॥
6.7.69: beautified by tresses strewn with many-coloured flowers, of a form pleasing in every respect, her face slightly bent with modesty, ॥69॥
6.7.70: holding a shining golden lotus in her right hand, having placed the other hand firmly upon a chowrie, seated on a comfortable seat. ॥70॥
6.7.71: Having thus meditated on me and on you, O Queen of gods, with a restrained mind, one should bathe us with water from the conch, following the order of sprinkling with the praṇava. ॥71॥
6.7.72: With bhave bhave nātibhave one should offer water for the feet; saying vāmāya namaḥ one should give water for sipping. ॥72॥
6.7.73: Saying jyeṣṭhāya namaḥ one should offer a white cloth; saying śreṣṭhāya namaḥ one should give the sacred thread. ॥73॥
6.7.74: Saying rudrāya namaḥ, one should give water for sipping again; saying kālāya namaḥ one should give well-prepared sandal paste. ॥74॥
6.7.75: With kalavikaraṇāya namaḥ one should offer unbroken rice; with balavikaraṇāya namaḥ one should offer flowers. ॥75॥
6.7.76: Saying balāya namaḥ one should carefully offer incense; with balapramathanāya one should offer a fine lamp. ॥76॥
6.7.77: With the Brahman mantras and the six aṅga mantras, then with the mātṛkā, with the praṇava, and with the Śiva mantra joined with Śakti, in due order, ॥77॥
6.7.78: one should display the mudrās to me and to you, O fair-complexioned one. One should offer the services first to me and then to you. ॥78॥
6.7.79: When performing them for you, one should then use the feminine gender. This alone is the difference, O Pārvatī; there is no other. ॥79॥
6.7.80: Having thus performed meditation and worship properly according to the rule, the wise one should begin the worship of my surrounding retinue (āvaraṇa). ॥80॥
6.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The description of meditation on Śiva and his worship, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
6.8.1: Īśvara said: Here, O Mahādevī, there is indeed a set of five enclosures (āvaraṇa). One should begin the worship of the five enclosures in due order. ॥1॥
6.8.2: Right where the two were first worshipped, the wise one should first worship in order, with fragrance and the rest, the two gods Heramba and Ṣaṇmukha. ॥2॥
6.8.3: He should then worship in order the five Brahman mantras around the circle: in the north-east, in the east, in the south, likewise in the north, ॥3॥
6.8.4: and in the west. Then, in that same circle, he should worship the six limbs (aṅga): in the south-east, likewise in the north-east, in the south-west, in the north-west region, ॥4॥
6.8.5: the eye in the middle, and likewise the weapon all around in order beginning from the east. The first enclosure has been described; now hear the second enclosure. ॥5॥
6.8.6: He should worship Ananta on the eastern petal, likewise Sūkṣma on the south, Śivottama on the west, and Ekanetra on the north, ॥6॥
6.8.7: likewise Ekarudra in the north-east, Trimūrti on the petal of the south-east, Śrīkaṇṭha in the south-west, and in the north-west he should worship Śikhaṇḍīśa. ॥7॥
6.8.8: In the second enclosure those sovereigns (cakravartin) are to be worshipped. In the middle of the eastern gate he should worship Vṛṣeśāna. ॥8॥
6.8.9: Nandin to its south and Mahākāla to its north; Bhṛṅgīśa he should worship to the west of the southern gate. ॥9॥
6.8.10: Having worshipped Vināyaka with fragrance and the rest in the compartment east of it, he should worship Vṛṣabha in the north-western compartment and Guha in the south. ॥10॥
6.8.11: To the east of the northern gate, following the clockwise procedure, he should worship by the method of the eight names; that is now stated. ॥11॥
6.8.12: Bhava, Śarva, likewise Īśāna, Rudra, then Paśupati, Ugra, Bhīma and Mahādeva: this is the third enclosure. ॥12॥
6.8.13: Having invoked Maheśvara with the mantra yo vedādau svaraḥ, he should worship him in the eastern part, on the pericarp of the lotus. ॥13॥
6.8.14: He should worship Īśvara on the eastern petal, then Viśveśa in the south, Parameśāna in the north and Sarveśa in the west. ॥14॥
6.8.15: In the south he should worship Rudra, having invoked him with the verse ā vo rājānam, with fragrance, flowers and the rest, on the pericarp and on the petals: ॥15॥
6.8.16: Śiva in the east, Hara in the south, Mṛḍa in the north and Bhava on the western petal: these are to be worshipped in due order. ॥16॥
6.8.17: In the north, having invoked Viṣṇu by reciting pra tad viṣṇuḥ, he should worship him with fragrance, flowers and the rest on the pericarp and on the petals: ॥17॥
6.8.18: He should worship Vāsudeva in the eastern part, Aniruddha in the south, Saṅkarṣaṇa in the north and Pradyumna in the west. ॥18॥
6.8.19: The knower of mantras should invoke and worship Brahmā on the western lotus with the mantra hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartata. ॥19॥
6.8.20: He should worship Hiraṇyagarbha in the east, then Virāj in the south, Puṣkara in the north and Kāla in the west. ॥20॥
6.8.21: In the outermost row, following the clockwise order beginning from the east, having worshipped the world-guardians (lokapāla) in succession in their respective places— ॥21॥
6.8.22: the syllables ending in ra, ending in ma, likewise ending in kṣa, ending in la, ending in va, the one not preceded by another, ending in sa, ending in ha, the first syllable of the Veda (Om) and the seed of Śrī: ten in order— ॥22॥
6.8.23: are the seed syllables of the world-guardians; with these he should worship them. In the south-west, likewise in the north, and to the south of Īśāna, ॥23॥
6.8.24: he should duly worship Brahmā and Viṣṇu with offerings. On the outer lines, O Queen of the gods, he should worship in the fifth enclosure: ॥24॥
6.8.25: he should worship the glorious trident in the north-east, the thunderbolt in the direction of great Indra (east), the axe in the region of Fire (south-east), and the arrow in Yama's quarter (south). ॥25॥
6.8.26: In the south-west he should worship the sword, the noose in Varuṇa's domain (west), the goad in the region of the Wind (north-west), and in the north he should worship the Pināka bow. ॥26॥
6.8.27: The one who knows the procedure should duly worship the fierce Kṣetrapāla facing west, solely for the pleasure of Śiva. ॥27॥
6.8.28: All of them are to be contemplated with palms joined in reverence, with lotus-faces smiling, and ever gazing respectfully at the god and the goddess. ॥28॥
6.8.29: Having thus performed the worship of the enclosures, in order to calm distractions he should worship the Lord of gods again and utter the praṇava and the name Śiva. ॥29॥
6.8.30: Having thus duly worshipped and served him with fragrance and other offerings, he should then offer food (naivedya) prepared according to rule. ॥30॥
6.8.31: Again he should give water for sipping (ācamana) and the arghya as before; then, as instructed, offer drinking water and betel. ॥31॥
6.8.32: Having performed the waving of lights (nīrājana) and the like, he should complete the remainder of the worship; meditating on the god and the goddess, he should repeat the mantra one hundred and eight times. ॥32॥
6.8.33: Then rising and standing with palms cupped holding flowers, meditating on Mahādeva, he should recite in order the hymn beginning yo devānām ॥33॥
6.8.34: up to the words yo vedādau svaraḥ proktaḥ, O Supreme Goddess. Then, having offered the handful of flowers, he should circumambulate three times. ॥34॥
6.8.35: Filled with supreme devotion, he should bow to him with the eight limbs touching the ground; having again circumambulated, he should once more bow a single time. ॥35॥
6.8.36: Seated on his seat, having worshipped the god with the eight names, he should say: Whatever act, good or bad, has been performed by me— ॥36॥
6.8.37: all that, O Lord Śambhu, is supreme worship of you. With these words he should offer it with conch-water together with a flower. ॥37॥
6.8.38: Having worshipped the Adorable One again, he should recite the eight names together with their meanings. Hear that very set, O Queen of the gods; I shall tell it to you because of your devotion. ॥38॥
6.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The description of the worship of the enclosures, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥8॥
6.9.1: Īśvara said: Śiva, Maheśvara, Rudra, Viṣṇu, Pitāmaha, Saṃsāravaidya (Physician of Worldly Existence), Sarvajña (All-knowing), and Paramātman (Supreme Self): these are the principal names. ॥1॥
6.9.2: This set of eight names always denotes Śiva. Of these, the first five correspond in order to Śāntyatītā and the rest. ॥2॥
6.9.3: They are the designations of Sadāśiva and the others, owing to the assumption of five limiting adjuncts (upādhi); but when the adjunct ceases, each designation ceases accordingly. ॥3॥
6.9.4: The office (pada) alone is eternal; those who hold the office are held to be non-eternal. There is a change of office-holders, since the holders become liberated. ॥4॥
6.9.5: Thus, in another cycle of change, again through his adjunct, the name would designate another soul; such is the first group of five names. ॥5॥
6.9.6: The other triad of names, however, arises from the distinction of material cause and the like; through the arrangement of the threefold adjunct it is Śiva alone who abides in them. ॥6॥
6.9.7: Because there is from the outset no contact with beginningless impurity, he is by nature a self utterly pure; hence he is called Śiva. ॥7॥
6.9.8: Or else, the Lord, being a single dense mass of all auspicious qualities, is called Śiva by the virtuous who know the meaning of the Śiva-principle. ॥8॥
6.9.9: Prakṛti is said to be beyond the twenty-three principles (tattva); beyond Prakṛti they declare the Puruṣa, the twenty-fifth. ॥9॥
6.9.10: It is that which they call the syllable (svara) at the beginning of the Veda, by the relation of denoted and denoter; knowable through the Veda alone in its true nature, and established in the Vedānta. ॥10॥
6.9.11: That very Puruṣa, merged in Prakṛti, is the enjoyer, since he enjoys Prakṛti; the one who is beyond him who is merged in Prakṛti, he is Maheśvara. ॥11॥
6.9.12: He is so called because the activity of Prakṛti and Puruṣa depends on him. Or else, this imperishable principle of three guṇas is māyā. ॥12॥
6.9.13: One should know Prakṛti as māyā and Maheśvara as the wielder of māyā. The Infinite one who releases from māyā is so through connection with Maheśvara. ॥13॥
6.9.14: Rud is sorrow, or the cause of sorrow; the Lord who drives that away is called Rudra. Hence Śiva is the supreme cause. ॥14॥
6.9.15: Śiva pervades and presides over everything from the Śiva-principle down to earth, bodies and the like, and pots and the like; hence he is called Viṣṇu. ॥15॥
6.9.16: Because Śiva is the father of all, even of those embodied beings who are the fathers of the world, he is declared Pitāmaha. ॥16॥
6.9.17: Just as a physician who knows the root cause removes a disease by remedies and medicines, so Śiva, the controller of dissolution, enjoyment and authority, ॥17॥
6.9.18: the Lord of saṃsāra, ever the remover of gross existence, is called Saṃsāravaidya by the knowers of the meaning of all principles. ॥18॥
6.9.19: Even though the sense organs exist for accomplishing the fivefold knowledge, the bound souls do not know the things of the three times, gross and subtle, in their entirety. ॥19॥
6.9.20: the bound souls (aṇu), covered by the impurity of the ocean of māyā, do not know. But even when all these senses are absent, Sadāśiva, knower of all things that are established, ॥20॥
6.9.21: Sadāśiva knows effortlessly every object exactly as it stands; therefore he is called Sarvajña. ॥21॥
6.9.22: Being the Self of all through eternal union with these supreme qualities, and since there is no self higher than himself, Śiva himself is Paramātman. ॥22॥
6.9.23: Having thus praised Mahādeva, the imperishable one whose self is the praṇava, and having offered arghya and pādya before him, then on the head of Īśāna, ॥23॥
6.9.24: having again worshipped the Lord of gods with the praṇava, concentrated, and taking the worship-flower with hands joined in añjali, ॥24॥
6.9.25: having led Śiva up to the Unmanī state by way of the left nostril, and then having dismissed the Goddess by way of the right nostril, ॥25॥
6.9.26: and having experienced oneness with him in the thought, I am Śiva alone, he should again dismiss all the deities of the enclosures (āvaraṇa) into the heart. ॥26॥
6.9.27: Having performed the worship of Vidyā and the worship of the guru, he should afterwards place in the heart, in due sequence, the mantras of the conch and the arghya vessel. ॥27॥
6.9.28: Then, having offered the used offerings (nirmālya) to Caṇḍīśa in the north-east (Īśa's quarter), and again with breath restrained, he should then recite the ṛṣi and the rest. ॥28॥
6.9.29: This maṇḍala, named Kailāsaprastara, has been described. One should worship it daily, or every fortnight, or every month, ॥29॥
6.9.30: or every six months, or yearly, or on festival occasions such as Cāturmāsya; but the believer must without fail worship my liṅga regularly. ॥30॥
6.9.31: In that procedure, O Great Goddess, a certain special point is told: on the day of initiation, the liṅga worshipped together with the guru ॥31॥
6.9.32: he should receive, saying, I shall worship Śiva until the end of my life, uttering this oath three times in the presence of the guru. ॥32॥
6.9.33: Then he should worship daily by the procedure stated earlier, O beloved, and offer arghya on the top of the liṅga with arghya water. ॥33॥
6.9.34: Having worshipped with the praṇava, he should offer incense and lamp; having worshipped Caṇḍa in the north-east, he should present the nirmālya to him. ॥34॥
6.9.35: Then, having washed the liṅga and the altar with water filtered through cloth, and having placed a flower on the top of the liṅga with the praṇava, ॥35॥
6.9.36: and having mentally contemplated everything from the Ādhāraśakti up to the seat of Śuddhavidyā, he should install the Supreme Lord. ॥36॥
6.9.37: With substances such as pañcagavya, gathered according to one's means, or with pure water alone scented with fragrant substances, ॥37॥
6.9.38: with the Pāvamāna, the Rudra, the Nīla and the Tvarita hymns, with Ṛk or Sāman verses, and with the five Brahma-mantras, ॥38॥
6.9.39: he should bathe the Lord of the gods of gods with the praṇava and the Śiva mantra; and he should also anoint him with the special arghya water, using the praṇava. ॥39॥
6.9.40: Having wiped it with a cloth, he should place a flower on the top of the liṅga; having set the liṅga on the pedestal, he should perform the worship of Sūrya and the others. ॥40॥
6.9.41: Below the seat (pīṭha) one should worship the two, Ādhāraśakti and Ananta; and above that, having worshipped the lion-throne in due order, ॥41॥
6.9.42: then one should worship the upper covering; at the foot of the seat one should worship Skanda. Having conceived my form in the liṅga, one should worship me together with you, ॥42॥
6.9.43: properly, with devotion and according to the rule — the ascetic intent on meditation on me. Thus I have told you this most secret teaching, O beloved. ॥43॥
6.9.44: It must be guarded with effort and not given to just anyone. It should be given to my devotee, to an ascetic free from passion, ॥44॥
6.9.45: devoted to the guru, tranquil, a partaker of yoga for my sake. Whoever, deluded in mind, transgresses my command and gives this to others, ॥45॥
6.9.46: he will go to hell and be my enemy; there is no doubt. But by giving it to my devotee, O Queen of the gods, one surely becomes dear to me; having enjoyed all pleasures here, he attains my presence. ॥46॥
6.9.47: Vyāsa said: Having heard this spoken by Mahādeva, the great Goddess praised the god with various hymns imbued with the meaning of the Vedas, ॥47॥
6.9.48: and the Supreme Goddess, bowing at the glorious lotus-feet of her husband, rejoiced with a heart overflowing with delight, O best of sages. ॥48॥
6.9.49: This, O brahmins, is most secret, revealing the meaning of the Praṇava; it is supreme in the knowledge of Śiva and destroys your afflictions. ॥49॥
6.9.50: Sūta said: Having spoken thus, the tiger among sages, Pārāśarya of great austerity, honoured with supreme devotion by the sages who expound the Veda, ॥50॥
6.9.51: recalling Mount Kailāsa, departed from that penance-grove. They too, with delighted hearts, at the end of the sacrificial session worshipped the Supreme Lord, ॥51॥
6.9.52: having worshipped with supreme devotion Soma (Śiva with Umā), who bears the half-moon as crest, they became devoted to yoga beginning with yama and intent on meditation on Śiva. ॥52॥
6.9.53: This was told by the Goddess to Guha, and by him to Nandin; and that blessed one declared it to the sage Sanatkumāra. ॥53॥
6.9.54: From him it was received by my guru Vyāsa of immeasurable splendour; and from him, O foremost sages, I too received this holy teaching. ॥54॥
6.9.55: I have made you hear this supreme teaching, more secret than the secret, dear to Giriśa, knowing you through your devotion to be dear to Śiva. ॥55॥
6.9.56: You too should give this secret, dear to Śiva, to ascetics of tranquil mind who are devoted to Śiva's feet. ॥56॥
6.9.57: Having said this, the greatly fortunate Sūta, best of Purāṇa-narrators, wandered over this earth on a pilgrimage to holy places. ॥57॥
6.9.58: Having received this supreme secret from Sūta, the lords among sages, dwelling in Kāśī itself, were liberated and went to the abode of Śiva. ॥58॥
6.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The description of the procedure concerning the meaning of the praṇava, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥9॥
6.10.1: Vyāsa said: Then, after Sūta had gone, the sages, greatly astonished, reflected among themselves: This has been forgotten: the doctrine of Vāmadeva that was set forth by the lord of sages. That is truly a hardship for us today. ॥1॥
6.10.2: When might we experience the sight of that excellent sage, which is supreme and removes the flood of sorrows of the ocean of worldly existence? Through the merit of worshipping Maheśvara, may the lord of sages now quickly appear before us. ॥2॥
6.10.3: Thus filled with anxious thought, the sages worshipped Vyāsa, the foremost of sages, in the lotus of their hearts, and remained eager to see him Sūta. ॥3॥
6.10.4: At the end of a year that great sage again reached Kāśī, devoted to Śiva-bhakti, wise, the illuminator of the meaning of the Purāṇas. ॥4॥
6.10.5: Seeing that Sūta approaching, the sages, delighted at heart, honoured him with the customary worship of rising to greet him, offering a seat, arghya water and so on. ॥5॥
6.10.6: He too, having smilingly greeted those tigers among sages, joyfully bathed in the supremely purifying water of the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā), ॥6॥
6.10.7: and having satisfied the sages, the gods and the ancestors with sesame and rice, he came to the bank, sprinkled himself, and put on two garments. ॥7॥
6.10.8: Having sipped water twice, having taken the ashes with the Sadyojāta and other mantras, and having applied them in the prescribed order beginning with smearing, the lord of sages then ॥8॥
6.10.9: adorned with a rudrākṣa garland, having performed his daily rites, the wise one drew the tripuṇḍra on the prescribed parts of the body according to rule. ॥9॥
6.10.10: He worshipped Viśveśvara, the beloved of Umā, together with his son and with the lord of the gaṇas, with true devotion, and praised him, bowing again and again. ॥10॥
6.10.11: Then, having worshipped Lord Kālabhairava according to rule, he circumambulated him, and again bowed three times and five times. ॥11॥
6.10.12: Again circumambulating and prostrating on the ground like a staff, he praised him with a supreme hymn, remembering his lotus feet. ॥12॥
6.10.13: Having recited the glorious five-syllable vidyā one thousand and eight times, standing before him, and having begged forgiveness of Maheśvara, ॥13॥
6.10.14: and then having worshipped Caṇḍīśa, he took the seat in the middle of the Mukti-maṇḍapa that was indicated to him by the sages who had mastered the Vedas. ॥14॥
6.10.15: When all were thus seated, having bowed with mantras, he then spoke words that increased the devotion of the chief sages. ॥15॥
6.10.16: Sūta said: Blessed are you, very wise sages of laudable vows. For your sake I have come here; hear this account of it. ॥16॥
6.10.17: After I had instructed you in the meaning of the Praṇava and went off on a pilgrimage to the sacred places, I now tell you that story. ॥17॥
6.10.18: Setting out from here, I reached the shore of the southern ocean, bathed, and duly worshipped the goddess Śivā in the form of a maiden (Kanyā); then, O chief brahmins, coming back to the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī, ॥18॥
6.10.19: in the most wonderful city named after the Śrī Kālahasti mountain, having bathed in the water of the Suvarṇamukharī, and offering libations to the gods and also the sages, ॥19॥
6.10.20: having duly satisfied them with devotion, joyfully remembering Giriśa, I worshipped Kālahastīśa, whose radiance equals that of the moonstone, ॥20॥
6.10.21: facing west, five-headed, most wonderful, who by a single sight alone is the cause of the destruction of all sins, ॥21॥
6.10.22: bestower of all siddhis, giver of enjoyment and liberation, lord of the three guṇas. And then with supreme devotion, I worshipped his Śivā standing at his right side, ॥22॥
