6.10.23: having worshipped Jñānaprasūnakalikā, the mother of the world, and the glorious five-syllable vidyā one thousand and eight times ॥23॥
6.10.24: having recited, I circumambulated, praised and bowed again and again. ॥24॥
6.10.25: Then, circumambulating the mountain every day with reverence, firm in my observances day after day, I rejoiced greatly, as it were, in my mind. ॥25॥
6.10.26: Thus, O lords of sages, I spent four months there by the grace of the great goddess Jñānaprasūnakalikā. ॥26॥
6.10.27: Once, having spread an excellent seat of cloth, deerskin and kuśa grass laid one upon another, the sage I, seated on it with senses restrained, ॥27॥
6.10.28: entering samādhi, a dense mass of supreme bliss and consciousness, with the conviction I am Śiva, perfectly full, I became one whose heart was wholly untroubled. ॥28॥
6.10.29: At that very moment my guru, an ocean of compassion, resembling a dark rain-cloud, bearing matted locks tawny as lightning, ॥29॥
6.10.30: tall, himself carrying a water-pot, a staff and a black deerskin, all his limbs white with ash, marked with every auspicious sign, ॥30॥
6.10.31: his forehead shining with the tripuṇḍra, his form adorned with rudrākṣas, his two eyes long and wide and reddish like lotus petals, ॥31॥
6.10.32: appeared swiftly in the lotus of my heart at that very moment. I was then bewildered — such was this marvel, O faithful ones. ॥32॥
6.10.33: Then, opening my eyes, I lamented, and my tears poured down like a mountain waterfall. ॥33॥
6.10.34: At that very moment a bodiless voice, most wondrous, was heard from the sky, O brahmins; listen to it attentively. ॥34॥
6.10.35: O son of Sūta, highly fortunate one, go to the city of Vārāṇasī. There are the sages whom you instructed before; now ॥35॥
6.10.36: they intensely long, helpless, for the blessing of your arrival; they remain without food. Having said this, it fell silent. ॥36॥
6.10.37: Then, rising quickly, I devoutly circumambulated the god and the goddess, and again prostrated on the ground like a staff ॥37॥
6.10.38: twelve times; then, understanding the command of my guru and of Śiva and Śivā, I left the sacred place quickly, and within forty days ॥38॥
6.10.39: I have arrived, O best of sages; may you favour me here. What should I speak about today? Tell me that. ॥39॥
6.10.40: Hearing these words of Sūta, the sages, delighted in mind, bowing again and again to Vyāsa, spoke to that tiger among sages. ॥40॥
6.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The teaching of Sūta, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
6.11.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, you are our supreme teacher. Therefore we question you, if we have your favour. ॥1॥
6.11.2: That teachers like you are always affectionate toward faithful disciples — this you have now shown us. ॥2॥
6.11.3: Formerly, at the time of the Virajā fire-offering, you alluded to the teaching of Vāmadeva, but we did not hear it in detail, O sage. ॥3॥
6.11.4: Now all of us wish to hear it with faith and the greatest reverence; O ocean of compassion, please relate it with kindness. ॥4॥
6.11.5: Hearing these words of theirs, Sūta, his hair bristling with joy, bowed to Mahādeva, the teacher higher than every teacher, ॥5॥
6.11.6: and to Mahādevī, mother of the three worlds, and devotedly to his teacher Vyāsa; then, in a deep voice, delighting the sages, he spoke this. ॥6॥
6.11.7: Sūta said: May all be well with you, O sages; may you always be happy — devotees of Śiva, steadfast in mind, promoters of devotion to Śiva. ॥7॥
6.11.8: That account, most wonderful indeed, I heard from the lotus-mouth of my teacher; I did not tell it before now, fearing to reveal a secret. ॥8॥
6.11.9: You are indeed most fortunate, devotees of Śiva, firm in your vows; having ascertained this, I shall tell you — listen with joy. ॥9॥
6.11.10: Long ago, in the Rathantara kalpa, the great sage Vāmadeva, liberated already in the womb, was himself the foremost teacher among the knowers of Śiva-knowledge. ॥10॥
6.11.11: He knew the true import of all scriptures — Vedas, Āgamas, Purāṇas and the rest — and knew the births and deeds of beings such as gods, demons and humans. ॥11॥
6.11.12: His whole body white with ash, adorned with a circle of matted locks, without shelter, free of desire, beyond the pairs of opposites, free of ego, ॥12॥
6.11.13: sky-clad, possessed of great wisdom, like a second Maheśvara, surrounded by eminent sages like himself who had become his disciples, ॥13॥
6.11.14: wandering over this earth, purifying it by the merit of the touch of his feet, his heart immersed day by day in the supreme abode, ॥14॥
6.11.15: joyfully entered Kumāra's Peak, south of Meru, where dwells the Lord, the son of Īśa, who rides the peacock, ॥15॥
6.11.16: the hero who bears the spear of knowledge, crusher of all asuras, accompanied by Gajāvallī, saluted by all the gods. ॥16॥
6.11.17: There is a lake named Skanda-saras, like an ocean, with cool, sweet water to drink, clear, deep and abundant, ॥17॥
6.11.18: endowed with every wondrous quality, lying near the Lord. Having bathed there with his disciples, the great sage Vāmadeva, ॥18॥
6.11.19: saw Kumāra seated on the peak, attended by hosts of sages, resplendent like the rising sun, having the excellent peacock as his mount, ॥19॥
6.11.20: four-armed, noble of form, adorned with a crown and other ornaments, worshipped by his two jewel-like consorts, holding the spear and the cock, ॥20॥
6.11.21: with hands in the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness — having seen Skanda, the lord of sages worshipped him with supreme devotion and began to praise him. ॥21॥
6.11.22: Vāmadeva said: Om, salutation to the meaning of the Praṇava, to the one who establishes the Praṇava's meaning, to the seed of the Praṇava syllable, to the Praṇava — salutation again and again. ॥22॥
6.11.23: Salutation again and again to the one whose form is the meaning of Vedānta, who expounds the meaning of Vedānta, who knows the meaning of Vedānta, and who is eternally known. ॥23॥
6.11.24: Salutation to Guha, who is hidden in the caves of the hearts of beings; to the secret one, whose form is secret, who knows the secret Āgamas. ॥24॥
6.11.25: Salutation to you, subtler than the subtle, greater even than the great, knower of the higher and the lower, whose nature is the Supreme Self. ॥25॥
6.11.26: Salutation always to Skanda, whose form is Skanda, whose splendour is ruddy like the sun, who wears a crown and other ornaments shining with mandāra garlands. ॥26॥
6.11.27: Salutation to the disciple of Śiva, the son of Śiva, the giver of auspiciousness, the beloved of Śiva, the treasure of bliss for Śiva and Śivā. ॥27॥
6.11.28: Salutation to you, son of Gaṅgā, Kārttikeya, the wise, the great son of Umā, who lay in the forest of reeds. ॥28॥
6.11.29: Salutation again and again to the six-faced one, whose body is the six-syllabled mantra, who establishes the sixfold meaning, whose form transcends the six paths. ॥29॥
6.11.30: To you with twelve wide eyes, with twelve raised arms, bearing twelve weapons — O twelvefold Self, salutation be to you. ॥30॥
6.11.31: Salutation to the four-armed, the peaceful, bearer of spear and cock, whose hands grant boons and fearlessness, the destroyer of asuras. ॥31॥
6.11.32: Salutation to him whose chest is marked with saffron smeared from Gajāvallī's breasts, whose self is gladdened by the joy and glory of Gajānana. ॥32॥
6.11.33: To you, abode of glory contemplated in purity through special songs sung by Brahmā and other gods, sages and Kinnaras; O you whose charming lotus-feet are worshipped with garlands adorning the spotless crowns of the gods — salutation be to you. ॥33॥
6.11.34: Whoever recites or even hears this divine hymn to Skanda spoken by Vāmadeva attains the supreme goal. ॥34॥
6.11.35: This indeed produces great wisdom, increases devotion to Śiva, brings long life, health and wealth, and always grants all desires. ॥35॥
6.11.36: Having thus praised the god, the Lord, the commander of the army, Vāmadeva circumambulated him three times and prostrated on the ground like a staff, ॥36॥
6.11.37: and again performing the eight-limbed prostration with circumambulation and salutation, he stood at his side, bowed in humility, O brahmins. ॥37॥
6.11.38: Hearing the hymn composed by Vāmadeva, unfolding the highest truth, the Lord, son of Maheśvara, became pleased. ॥38॥
6.11.39: Mahāsena said to him: I am pleased with your worship, devotion and praise. Blessings to you. What shall I do for you today? ॥39॥
6.11.40: O sage, you are the foremost of yogins, wholly fulfilled and free of desire; for such as you there is indeed nothing in this world to be sought. ॥40॥
6.11.41: Even so, for the protection of dharma and out of a wish to favour the worlds, good and holy men like you wander over the earth. ॥41॥
6.11.42: If there is something you wish to hear, O brahmin, you should state it now; then I shall now explain it for the sake of favouring the worlds. ॥42॥
6.11.43: Having heard these words of Skanda, the great sage Vāmadeva, bowed down in humility, spoke in a voice deep as a rain-cloud. ॥43॥
6.11.44: Vāmadeva said: O Lord, you are the supreme ruler, the bestower of both higher and lower glories, omniscient, the maker of all, the bearer of all powers, the master. ॥44॥
6.11.45: We are mere embodied souls, unfit to speak in the presence of you, the supreme ruler; yet it is your grace that you speak to me. ॥45॥
6.11.46: O greatly wise one, I am fulfilled by even a mere particle of your knowledge. Urged on, I ask further; my transgression should be forgiven. ॥46॥
6.11.47: The praṇava is indeed supreme, directly the word that denotes the Supreme Lord; what it denotes is the god Paśupati, who releases the bound souls (paśu) from their fetter. ॥47॥
6.11.48: Invoked by the denoting word, he frees the bound souls in an instant; therefore the praṇava is established as the word denoting Śiva. ॥48॥
6.11.49: Om — all this is Om, says the eternal Veda; and it declared, Om is Brahman; all this indeed is Brahman. ॥49॥
6.11.50: Salutation to you, commander of the gods' army, lord of the gods; salutation to the lord of ascetics; salutation to you, the all-complete. ॥50॥
6.11.51: This being so, in this world nothing exists other than Śiva; the master who bears all forms is Śiva, the all-pervading Maheśvara. ॥51॥
6.11.52: I have heard the meaning of the praṇava in terms of its collective and individual aspects; but never, O Mahāsena, have I found a teacher like you. ॥52॥
6.11.53: Therefore, showing compassion, you should explain that meaning by the method of formal instruction and in accordance with the order of right conduct. ॥53॥
6.11.54: You are the sole master of all beings, the teacher who cuts their fetters; therefore, O teacher, that meaning must be heard by me through your grace. ॥54॥
6.11.55: Thus questioned by the sage, Skanda bowed to Sadāśiva, whose body is the praṇava, marked by the excellent thirty-eight kalās, with Umā ever at his side and attended by the foremost sages, and began to expound the supreme good, hidden even in the Vedas. ॥55॥
6.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The description of Brahman to Vāmadeva, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
6.12.1: Śrī Brahmaṇya said: Excellent, excellent, O greatly fortunate Vāmadeva, lord of sages! You are exceedingly devoted to Śiva and the best among those who possess knowledge of Śiva. ॥1॥
6.12.2: There is nothing anywhere in the worlds that is unknown to you; even so, I shall speak to you, who work for the benefit of the worlds. ॥2॥
6.12.3: In this world all bound souls (paśus) are deluded by various scriptures, deceived by the exceedingly wondrous māyā of the Supreme Lord. ॥3॥
6.12.4: They do not know Maheśvara, the Supreme, who is directly the meaning of the Praṇava — Brahman with and without attributes, the supreme progenitor of the three gods. ॥4॥
6.12.5: Raising my right arm, I declare an oath to you: it is true, true, again true; true, true, again and again. ॥5॥
6.12.6: Śiva himself is proclaimed as principally the meaning of the Praṇava in the Śrutis, in the Smṛti treatises, in the Purāṇas and in the Āgamas. ॥6॥
6.12.7: He from whom words turn back, together with the mind, without reaching him; knowing whose bliss the wise one fears nothing from anywhere. ॥7॥
6.12.8: From whom this entire universe, beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Indra, together with the groups of elements and senses, is first brought forth; ॥8॥
6.12.9: Who indeed is never born from anything at any time; in whom neither lightning shines, nor the sun, nor the moon; ॥9॥
6.12.10: By whose light this whole universe shines on all sides; endowed with all lordship, he himself is by name Sarveśvara (Lord of all). ॥10॥
6.12.11: Śambhu, who is to be meditated upon by those seeking liberation, abiding in the midst of the inner space, all-pervading, self-luminous, of the form of radiance, consisting of consciousness; ॥11॥
6.12.12: Of which Person the supreme Śakti is attainable through devotion, enchanting, without attributes, concealed by her own qualities, partless and auspicious (Śivā). ॥12॥
6.12.13: His form is threefold: gross, subtle, and then the supreme. O sage, it is to be meditated upon constantly and in sequence by yogins seeking liberation. ॥13॥
6.12.14: He who is partless, the eternal primal god of all gods, whose nature is knowledge and action, is sung of as the Supreme Self. ॥14॥
6.12.15: The embodied form of that God of gods is Sadāśiva himself, the god whose body is the five mantras and whose figure is the set of five kalās. ॥15॥
6.12.16: Resembling pure crystal, serene, of cool radiance, the Lord has five faces, ten arms and fifteen eyes. ॥16॥
6.12.17: The ancient one has Īśāna as his crown, Tatpuruṣa as his face, Aghora as his heart, and Vāmadeva as his secret parts; ॥17॥
6.12.18: and Sadyojāta as his feet. That form is directly both with parts and partless; his body is made of six limbs consisting of the six powers beginning with omniscience. ॥18॥
6.12.19: He is resplendent with a heart-lotus pulsing with the powers beginning with sound, and adorned on his left side by his own Śakti, Manonmanī. ॥19॥
6.12.20: By way of setting forth the meanings of the six kinds of meaning beginning with the mantra, I shall explain the sense of the collective and individual aspects, which is of the nature of the Praṇava. ॥20॥
6.12.21: First, the order of instruction must be stated; listen to it. O sage, the four-class order is well known in this human world. ॥21॥
6.12.22: Here, conformity to Vedic practice belongs only to the three twice-born classes; the Śūdras, whose essential duty is service alone, are excluded from the Veda. ॥22॥
6.12.23: For all members of the three classes, devoted to their respective stages of life, the dharma declared in Śruti and Smṛti is to be practised, and never any other. ॥23॥
6.12.24: Performing the action enjoined by Śruti and Smṛti, one will attain perfection — so declared the Supreme Lord, who reveals the Vedic path. ॥24॥
6.12.25: Having worshipped the Supreme Lord through the merits of the conduct of their class and stage of life, many excellent sages have all attained union (sāyujya) with him. ॥25॥
6.12.26: The sages are satisfied by celibate study, the gods by the path of sacrificial rites, the ancestors by progeny — so indeed the Śruti has said. ॥26॥
6.12.27: Thus freed from the three debts, having entered the forest-dweller stage, enduring cold and heat, pleasure and pain and the like, with senses subdued, ॥27॥
6.12.28: an ascetic with controlled diet should practise yoga beginning with yama, so that his understanding becomes very firm and unshakable. ॥28॥
6.12.29: Thus, purified in self by stages, he should lay aside all actions; having renounced all actions, he should become devoted to the worship of knowledge. ॥29॥
6.12.30: For that worship directly grants the fruit of liberation-in-life through oneness with Śiva; it should be known as the highest of all, changeless, for the self-controlled. ॥30॥
6.12.31: I shall describe its procedure out of desire to benefit the world and out of affection for you, O greatly wise one; listen attentively. ॥31॥
6.12.32: That ascetic should approach a preceptor who knows the essence of the meaning of all scriptures, who has mastered the knowledge of Vedānta, the best among the wise. ॥32॥
6.12.33: Going near him according to rule, the discerning, wise one should diligently please him with full-length prostrations and the like. ॥33॥
6.12.34: He who is the guru is declared to be Śiva; he who is Śiva is held to be the guru — having resolved this in his mind, he should make known his intention. ॥34॥
6.12.35: Having obtained permission from the guru, he should observe a milk-only vow for twelve days, and then, according to rule, on the fourth or the tenth day of the bright fortnight, ॥35॥
6.12.36: having bathed at dawn, pure in self, having performed his daily rites, the wise one should invite the guru and begin the Nāndī-śrāddha according to rule. ॥36॥
6.12.37: The Viśvedevas are declared to be those named Satya and Vasu; in the Deva-śrāddha, the three — Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa — are mentioned. ॥37॥
6.12.38: In the Ṛṣi-śrāddha, the sages born among the gods, of the holy fields and among men are declared; and in the Deva-śrāddha, the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas are proclaimed. ॥38॥
6.12.39: In the human śrāddha, the four lords of sages beginning with Sanaka; in the Bhūta-śrāddha, the five great elements, and after that, ॥39॥
6.12.40: the group of senses beginning with the eye, and the fourfold class of beings; in the Pitṛ-śrāddha, the three: the father, his father, and his father. ॥40॥
6.12.41: In the śrāddha for the mothers, the recipients are the mother, the paternal grandmother and the great-grandmother. In the śrāddha for oneself there are four: oneself, the father and the grandfather, ॥41॥
6.12.42: and the one called the great-grandfather; these are declared to be honoured together with their wives. In the śrāddha for the maternal grandfathers there are three: the maternal grandfather and the others. ॥42॥
6.12.43: For each śrāddha, having arranged the invited brāhmaṇas in pairs, having called them, washed their feet, and having himself carefully sipped water, ॥43॥
6.12.44: May the dust of the brāhmaṇas' feet purify me — dust that is the cause of attaining all prosperity, a comet of destruction to the host of calamities that have arisen, a bridge across the shoreless ocean of saṃsāra. ॥44॥
6.12.45: May the dust of the brāhmaṇas' feet protect me — dust that is a thousand-rayed sun to the darkness of the dense cloud of calamity, a wish-granting cow bestowing desired objects, whose form is pure like the waters of all the holy places. ॥45॥
6.12.46: Having muttered this and bowed with all eight limbs on the ground like a staff, standing facing east, remembering the pair of lotus-feet of Śambhu, ॥46॥
6.12.47: with the kuśa-ring in his hand, pure, wearing the sacred thread, firm in his seat, he should perform three breath-controls, having again heard the statement of the lunar day and so on, and resolve: ॥47॥
6.12.48: That which is a component of my saṃnyāsa — the eightfold śrāddha beginning with the Viśvedevas and ending with the maternal grandfathers — by the pārvaṇa method, ॥48॥
6.12.49: I shall perform according to rule, with your permission preceding. Having made the resolve thus, he should cast away the darbha grass to the north. ॥49॥
6.12.50: Having touched water and risen, he should begin the sequence of choosing the brāhmaṇas. With the kuśa-ring in hand, touching the hands of the two brāhmaṇas, he should say: ॥50॥
6.12.51: For the sake of the Viśvedevas, and so on, and also, the occasion be granted by you two, ॥51॥
6.12.52: ending with, is to be graciously granted. This is the order of procedure in every case. Having thus completed the choosing, he should prepare the maṇḍalas, ॥52॥
6.12.53: ten of them, beginning from the north, and having worshipped them with unbroken rice, having seated the brāhmaṇas in them in order, again at their feet ॥53॥
6.12.54: he should utter the names of the Viśvedevas and the rest in the vocative, saying, This is water for your feet, with water containing kuśa, flowers and unbroken rice. ॥54॥
6.12.55: Having offered the foot-water, himself also with feet washed, facing north, having sipped water, and having seated those brāhmaṇas arranged in pairs on their seats, ॥55॥
6.12.56: having given a seat of darbha, saying, This is the seat for the brāhmaṇa who is in the form of the Viśvedevas, he himself, standing with darbha in hand, ॥56॥
6.12.57: having said, In this Nāndīmukha śrāddha, for the sake of the Viśvedevas, the occasion is to be granted by you two, should say, let it be done. ॥57॥
6.12.58: Having declared, may it obtain, he should say, you two, so that it runs, may you two obtain; and those two eminent brāhmaṇas should reply, may we two obtain. ॥58॥
6.12.59: Saying to them, May it be complete, may there be fulfilment of the resolve, he should entreat the eminent twice-born: May you favour me. ॥59॥
6.12.60: Then, in clean, washed vessels of plantain-leaf and the like, having served rice and other edibles, and separately with darbha, ॥60॥
6.12.61: having himself spread them around there and sprinkled water around, then respectfully holding each vessel with both hands, ॥61॥
6.12.62: having recited, The earth is your vessel, and so on, and naming in the dative the deities and others stationed there, together with unbroken rice, ॥62॥
6.12.63: taking water towards the north, he should then offer the food for the deity with svāhā; at the end he should say, not mine. This is the order of procedure everywhere. ॥63॥
6.12.64: I salute that Lord accompanied by Ambā, by remembering whose lotus-feet and even by muttering whose name a deficient rite becomes complete. ॥64॥
6.12.65: Having muttered this, he should then say: This Nāndīmukha śrāddha has been performed by me, and thereafter say as prescribed. ॥65॥
6.12.66: and, Please say, so be it; having propitiated those eminent twice-born, releasing the water held in his hand, and prostrating on the ground like a staff, ॥66॥
6.12.67: and having risen, he should then say to the brāhmaṇas, May it be nectar, and, noble-minded, with joined palms, he should entreat them with great affection. ॥67॥
6.12.68: Meditating on Sadāśiva in his mind, he should recite according to rule the Śrī Rudra, the Camaka, the Puruṣa Sūkta, and the five Brahman mantras. ॥68॥
6.12.69: At the end of the meal he should recite the Rudra Sūkta and again ask pardon of the brāhmaṇas; then with its mantra he should offer before them the concluding sip of water (uttarāpośana). ॥69॥
6.12.70: With feet washed, having sipped water, he should then go to the place of the piṇḍas; seated facing east, silent, he should perform three breath-controls, ॥70॥
6.12.71: resolving: I shall perform the offering of piṇḍas, a component of the śrāddha called Nāndīmukha. Having made this resolve, beginning from the south up to the north, ॥71॥
6.12.72: having drawn nine lines, and having spread twelve darbha blades in order with tips to the east, he should prepare the five places of the deities and others beginning from the south. ॥72॥
6.12.73: Silently he should offer water with unbroken rice in three places in order; in the other places, for the mothers, with the words mārjayantām thereafter. ॥73॥
6.12.74: Afterwards, with Here, O Fathers (atra pitaraḥ), having worshipped with water and unbroken rice, he should then offer in order in the five places of the deities and others, ॥74॥
6.12.75: and, uttering the names of the respective deities and others with the dative ending, he should then offer three piṇḍas in each of the five places. ॥75॥
6.12.76: He should offer the piṇḍas separately by the method stated in his own Gṛhyasūtra, and he should offer this with unbroken rice for the sake of the ancestors' fulfilment. ॥76॥
6.12.77: He should meditate on the god Sadāśiva in the centre of the lotus of the heart, again reciting the verse beginning By remembering whose lotus-feet. ॥77॥
6.12.78: Having bowed to the brāhmaṇas and given them a fee according to his means, having asked their pardon and dismissed them, then in due order, ॥78॥
6.12.79: having removed the piṇḍas, he should give them as a mouthful for a cow, or else cast them into water. Having performed the puṇyāhavācana, he should eat together with his kinsmen. ॥79॥
6.12.80: On the next day, rising at dawn, the wise man, having performed his daily rites and having fasted, should undergo shaving and the rest, excluding the armpits and the private parts. ॥80॥
6.12.81: Having removed the hair of the head, the beard and the nails, as the limit of the rite requires, and having had all the hair shaved properly, in accordance with the prescribed rule, ॥81॥
6.12.82: having bathed, wearing a washed cloth, pure, having sipped water twice, then restraining his speech, having applied holy ash according to rule and having performed the puṇyāha-vācana, the proclamation of the auspicious day, ॥82॥
6.12.83: having sprinkled himself with that water and thereby attained the natural state of a purified body, and having set aside what is needed for the materials of the fire-offering and for the preceptor's fee, ॥83॥
6.12.84: having then given away the rest of his possessions to Maheśa, and especially to the twice-born and to devotees, and to Śiva in the form of the guru, ॥84॥
6.12.85: having given a fee of clothes and the like, and bowed down on the ground like a staff, then taking the waist-string, loincloth, garment, staff and the rest, washed, placed on the ground, ॥85॥
6.12.86: and taking in due order the materials for the fire-offering, the fuel-sticks and the rest, — on a seashore, by a river, on a mountain, or in a temple of Śiva, ॥86॥
6.12.87: or in a forest, or in a cow-pen — having chosen an excellent spot, standing there and sipping water, then first performing the mental offering (mānasa-mañjarī), ॥87॥
6.12.88: having muttered three times the brāhma mantra together with Oṃkāra, and also namo brahmaṇe, salutation to Brahman, he should then recite agnim īḷe purohitam, the opening of the Ṛgveda, ॥88॥
6.12.89: then atha mahāvratam, and agnir vai devānām, and likewise the corpus of this Veda, iṣe tvorje tvā, the opening of the Yajurveda, ॥89॥
6.12.90: agna āyāhi vītaye, the opening of the Sāmaveda, śaṃ no devīr abhiṣṭaye, the opening of the Atharvaveda; afterwards he should recite the prosody formula with ma, ya, ra, sa, ta, ja, bha, na, la and ga, ॥90॥
6.12.91: then sammitam, then pañcasaṃvatsaramayam, the Jyotiṣa, then samāmnāyaḥ samāmnātaḥ, the Nirukta; then again he should recite the Śikṣā, uttering pravakṣyāmi (I shall expound), and then recite vṛddhir ādaic, Pāṇini's grammar. ॥91॥
6.12.92: Having uttered athāto dharmajijñāsā, the opening of the Mīmāṃsā-sūtra, and again promptly athāto brahmajijñāsā, the opening of the Brahma-sūtra, he should also mutter the beginnings of the Vedas and the rest. ॥92॥
6.12.93: Then the names Brahmā, Indra, Sūrya, Soma and Prajāpati, the Self, the inner Self, the knowledge-Self, and beyond that ॥93॥
6.12.94: and also the Supreme Self — having muttered each name in the dative case, beginning with Praṇava and ending with namaḥ, he should then take a handful of barley-meal ॥94॥
6.12.95: and having eaten it with the Praṇava alone, and having sipped water twice, he should touch his navel while reciting the mantras about to be stated, beginning with Praṇava and ending with namaḥ: ॥95॥
6.12.96: having uttered the Self, the inner Self, the knowledge-Self, again the supreme, and the Self, and after that Prajāpati, ॥96॥
6.12.97: he should then mutter these mantras ending with svāhā. Afterwards, having partaken of milk, curd and ghee separately, three times each with the Praṇava alone, he should again sip water twice. ॥97॥
6.12.98: Then, sitting down facing east, with a firm mind and a steady posture, he should properly perform three breath-controls according to the rule already stated. ॥98॥
6.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The description of the rite of saṃnyāsa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
6.13.1: Subrahmaṇya said: Then at midday, having bathed, with a controlled mind, one should bring the articles of worship: sandal paste, flowers, unbroken rice and the rest. ॥1॥
6.13.2: In the south-west one should worship the god Vighneśa, who is worshipped by the gods; one should invoke him with the mantra gaṇānāṃ tvā according to proper rule. ॥2॥
6.13.3: He is red in colour, huge in body, adorned with all ornaments, holding in his lotus-hands the noose, the goad, the rosary and the boon-granting gesture. ॥3॥
6.13.4: Having thus invoked and meditated upon the elephant-faced son of Śambhu, and having worshipped him with milk-rice, cakes, coconut, jaggery and the like, ॥4॥
6.13.5: one should offer excellent food-offering, and then betel and other things; having pleased him and bowed, one should then pray for freedom from obstacles. ॥5॥
6.13.6: In the aupāsana fire, according to the procedure stated in one's own Gṛhya-sūtra, the fire-rite up to the ājyabhāga offerings should be performed, and after this the main procedure of the sacrifice. ॥6॥
6.13.7: Having offered the full oblation with the three verses beginning bhūḥ svāhā and having concluded, one should, untiring, repeat the Gāyatrī until the afternoon. ॥7॥
6.13.8: Then, having performed the evening twilight worship preceded by a bath, and having offered the evening aupāsana, remaining silent, one should inform the guru. ॥8॥
6.13.9: Having cooked the caru in that fire, one should offer, with fuel-sticks, food and ghee separately, with the Raudra Sūkta and the five mantras beginning with Sadyojāta, ॥9॥
6.13.10: and with the Brahma-mantras; one should contemplate Mahādeva together with Ambā in the fire. Having offered with the mantra gaurīr mimāya, remembering Gaurī, ॥10॥
6.13.11: then one should offer once with agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā. Having performed the concluding procedure, the wise one, then, to the north of the fire, ॥11॥
6.13.12: seated on a seat overspread with cloth, deerskin and kuśa grass, silent and firm of mind, should repeat the Gāyatrī until the Brāhma muhūrta. ॥12॥
6.13.13: Then, having bathed, or if unable, bathing with ash according to rule, having cooked the caru in that same fire, sprinkled with ghee, ॥13॥
6.13.14: having removed it to the north, placed it on the sacred grass and then sprinkled the caru with ghee, he should recite the vyāhṛtis, the Raudra Sūkta and the five ॥14॥
6.13.15: Brahma-mantras, fixing the mind on the lotus-feet of Śiva. Then Prajāpati, then Indra, and after that the Viśvedevas, ॥15॥
6.13.16: and Brahmā — in the dative, ending with svāhā and beginning with praṇava — having recited these and then having had the puṇyāha benediction recited, thereafter, ॥16॥
6.13.17: having completed the subsequent procedure from agnaye svāhā up to the agnimukha, afterwards, beginning with prāṇāya svāhā, with the five, ॥17॥
6.13.18: with caru mixed with ghee; afterwards he should offer to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. And again he should recite the Raudra Sūkta and the five Brahma-mantras. ॥18॥
6.13.19: And again he should recite the mantras of the fourfold manifestation beginning with Maheśa. Having performed the concluding procedure by the method stated in one's own Vedic branch, ॥19॥
6.13.20: the discerning one should perform it with its subsidiary parts, directing it to the respective deities. Thus is the ritual procedure, beginning with the agnimukha, which has been set forth. ॥20॥
6.13.21: After this he should offer the Virajā homa for himself, for the purification of the self merged in this body consisting of the twenty-six tattvas, ॥21॥
6.13.22: remembering, May these tattvas in my body be purified. There, for the purification of the ātma-tattva, with the mantras of the Āruṇaketuka section, ॥22॥
6.13.23: being recited, in order from earth up to puruṣa, O sage, with caru mixed with ghee, silent, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva. ॥23॥
6.13.24: Earth and the rest, sound and the rest, again the pentad beginning with speech, the pentad beginning with the ear, and the group of four — head, sides, back and belly — ॥24॥
6.13.25: and the shanks one should add; then the seven bodily constituents beginning with skin; then the pentad beginning with prāṇa; then the five sheaths beginning with the food-sheath; ॥25॥
6.13.26: mind, citta, intellect, ego, khyāti and saṅkalpa; then the guṇas, then prakṛti, and then puruṣa. ॥26॥
6.13.27: For the puruṣa, who has attained the state of enjoyer in the act of enjoyment, a pentad of tattvas is declared as the inner instrument. ॥27॥
6.13.28: Niyati, kāla, rāga, then vidyā, and kalā — this pentad, O lord of sages, has arisen from Māyā. ॥28॥
6.13.29: One should know Māyā to be Prakṛti — thus Māyā is spoken of in the śruti. These tattvas born of her are stated in the śruti; there is no doubt. ॥29॥
6.13.30: Time, inherent nature, niyati — so too the śruti declared. This very pentad is called his five sheaths (kañcukas). ॥30॥
6.13.31: Not knowing these five tattvas, even a learned man is deluded in mind. This puruṣa, placed below these five and above prakṛti, ॥31॥
6.13.32: resorting to the maxim of the crow's eye, abides daily at the side of both. This is called the vidyā-tattva. Śuddhavidyā, Maheśvara, ॥32॥
6.13.33: Sadāśiva, Śakti and Śiva — this pentad is the Śiva-tattva, O Brahman; it is prajñānaṃ brahma, meditated upon by one restrained in speech. ॥33॥
6.13.34: The whole group of tattvas from earth up to Śiva, O lord of sages — let its purification be effected through dissolution into its own cause. ॥34॥
6.13.35: For the eleven mantras, preceded by the word parasmai, one should then utter this word śivajyotiṣe in the dative. ॥35॥
6.13.36: Afterwards he should say na mama (not mine); this is called the renunciation of the dedicated offering. After this, for the two mantras viviḍḍhi and kaṣotkāya, ॥36॥
6.13.37: at the end of the word vyāpakāya he should add also paramātmane, śivajyotiṣe in the dative, and again the word viśvabhūta, ॥37॥
6.13.38: and then he should say the word ghasanotsuka in the dative; having uttered parasmai, he should utter the word devāya. ॥38॥
6.13.39: For the mantra uttiṣṭhasva, after the word viśvarūpāya he should say the word puruṣāya, and for it he should pronounce oṃ svāhā. ॥39॥
6.13.40: After the word loka-traya (the three worlds), he should then say the words: To the all-pervading Supreme Self, to Śiva, this is offered, not mine. ॥40॥
6.13.41: Having completed the preliminary rites in the manner prescribed by his own Vedic branch, and having eaten the caru mixed with ghee, to the priest ॥41॥
6.13.42: he should give to him a fee augmented with gold and other things. Then, having dismissed the Brahmā priest, he should perform the morning aupāsana oblation. ॥42॥
6.13.43: The man should recite the mantra saṃ mā siñcantu marutaḥ; and with the mantra yā te agne, having warmed his hand in the fire, ॥43॥
6.13.44: having placed his hand over the fire and taken the fire up into his own self, the abode of non-duality; then having performed the morning twilight worship, and then also worshipping the sun, ॥44॥
6.13.45: having attended upon the sun, entering the water and immersing himself up to the navel, he should recite those mantras with devotion, with steady mind and eager. ॥45॥
6.13.46: But one who maintains the sacred fires should properly perform the Prājāpatya sacrifice in the established śrauta Vaiśvānara fire, with a fee of all his possessions. ॥46॥
6.13.47: Then, having taken the fire into himself, the brāhmaṇa should go forth from home. Having uttered the first pāda of the Sāvitrī and the word sāvitrīm, ॥47॥
6.13.48: he should say bhūḥ om after the word praveśayāmi (I make enter). Having uttered the second pāda and sāvitrīm as before, ॥48॥
6.13.49: he should say bhūḥ om after the word praveśayāmi. Having uttered the third pāda, and after that sāvitrīm, ॥49॥
6.13.50: he should utter suvaḥ om after the word praveśayāmi. First he should utter the three pādas together, and after that sāvitrīm, ॥50॥
6.13.51: and after the word praveśayāmi he should then utter bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar om with devotion, with a steady mind, O lord of sages. ॥51॥
6.13.52: This Goddess is in very truth the one who forms half of Śaṅkara's body; she has five faces, ten arms, and shines with fifteen eyes. ॥52॥
6.13.53: She wears as crest-ornament the crescent moon rising on a crown of nine gems; she resembles pure crystal, bears ten weapons, and is auspicious. ॥53॥
6.13.54: Her limbs are adorned with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, girdle-bells, anklets and the like; she wears divine garments and jewelled ornaments. ॥54॥
6.13.55: She is always to be served by Viṣṇu, by Brahmā, by gods, sages, Gandharvas, Dānavas and men; she is Śivā, who pervades the selves of all. ॥55॥
6.13.56: She is the charming lawful wife of the god Sadāśiva, Mother of the world, Mother of the three worlds/deities, possessing the three guṇas yet free of guṇas, and unborn. ॥56॥
6.13.57: Having reflected thus, the wise one should then recite the Gāyatrī, the primordial Goddess, three-footed, unborn, who bestows brāhmaṇahood and the rest. ॥57॥
6.13.58: The sinner who recites the Gāyatrī, whose form is Śiva, otherwise than thus is cooked in a most terrible hell for a period of kalpas. ॥58॥
6.13.59: She arose from the vyāhṛtis and dissolves into them alone; and they arose from the Praṇava and dissolve into the Praṇava. ॥59॥
6.13.60: The Praṇava is the beginning of all the Vedas; the Praṇava denotes Śiva. It is the king of the kings of mantras, the great seed, the supreme mantra. ॥60॥
6.13.61: Śiva indeed is this Praṇava, or the Praṇava is declared to be Śiva, since there is no absolute difference between the denoted and that which denotes. ॥61॥
6.13.62: By causing beings who are leaving the body at death in Kāśī to hear this very great mantra, Śiva grants them supreme liberation. ॥62॥
6.13.63: Therefore the best of ascetics worship the one-syllabled god Śiva, the supreme cause, abiding in the middle of the heart-lotus. ॥63॥
6.13.64: Other steadfast seekers of liberation, and worldly men who have become dispassionate, having understood sense-objects with the mind, worship the supreme Śiva. ॥64॥
6.13.65: Having thus dissolved the Gāyatrī into the Praṇava, which denotes Śiva, he should then recite the anuvāka ahaṃ vṛkṣasya rerivā. ॥65॥
6.13.66: Reciting the anuvāka yaś chandasām ṛṣabhaḥ from its beginning up to its end with gopāya, he should afterwards say utthito'ham (I have arisen). ॥66॥
6.13.67: He should say and recite it three times, in low, middle and high tone in succession, O sage, first uttering the Praṇava, in the order of creation, maintenance and dissolution. ॥67॥
6.13.68: Then in order among them: bhūḥ saṃnyastam, likewise bhuvaḥ saṃnyastam, and having said suvaḥ saṃnyastam, uttering the word saṃnyastam, ॥68॥
6.13.69: at the end of all the mantras he should say the word mayā (by me). First uttering the Praṇava, he should say the vyāhṛtis together, ॥69॥
6.13.70: after that he should say samastam and mayā — so it has been declared — having meditated on Sadāśiva in the heart, then in the order of low tone and so on, O sage. ॥70॥
6.13.71: Having thus recited the praiṣa mantras with an attentive mind, reciting, Freedom from fear to all beings from me, svāhā, ॥71॥
6.13.72: taking up water toward the eastern direction, he should then cast out a handful. Then, pulling out the topknot and the sacred thread with his hand, ॥72॥
6.13.73: and holding them, he should say, Om bhūḥ, go to the ocean, uttering svāhā (Agni's wife); then with a handful of water ॥73॥
6.13.74: he should offer them into the water. Then, having consecrated water three times with the praiṣa mantras and sipped it, he should come to the bank and leave his clothes and other things on the ground. ॥74॥
6.13.75: Facing north or east, he should walk more than seven steps, some distance; then the teacher should say, Stop, stop. ॥75॥
6.13.76: For the sake of worldly conduct, he should give with his own hand a loincloth and a staff, saying, Revered one, accept these. ॥76॥
6.13.77: Having given the loincloth with a good string and then the ochre garment, and the disciple having covered himself and sipped water twice, he should address that disciple thus: ॥77॥
6.13.78: Then he should pronounce the mantra indrasya vajro'si (you are Indra's thunderbolt). Having made the request, the disciple should take the staff, reciting sakhāyaḥ. ॥78॥
6.13.79: Then, going to the side of the guru and remembering Śiva's lotus feet, he should prostrate on the ground like a staff three times, with self-restraint. ॥79॥
6.13.80: And rising again slowly, gazing with love at his own guru, he should stand near the guru's feet with his palms joined in reverence. ॥80॥
6.13.81: Even before the rite begins, he should take auspicious cow-dung, make it into balls the size of a large āmalaka fruit, and dry them, ॥81॥
6.13.82: by the rays of the sun alone. Placing them in the midst of the fire at the start of the homa, at the completion of the homa he should collect the ash and keep it safe. ॥82॥
6.13.83: Then the guru, taking the white ash produced from the Virajā fire, with that very ash, in due order, with the mantras beginning agniḥ, ॥83॥
6.13.84: touching the disciple's limbs with these mantras from the head down to the feet, and then with the five mantras beginning with Īśāna, starting from the head, all over the body, ॥84॥
6.13.85: having smeared the ash according to rule, he should then make him wear the tripuṇḍra, with the tryāyuṣa and tryambaka mantras, beginning from the head in due order. ॥85॥
6.13.86: Then the excellent disciple, with a mind filled with true devotion, should meditate on Śiva, the companion of Umā, seated in the lotus of his heart. ॥86॥
6.13.87: Placing his hand on the disciple's head, the guru should utter the praṇava three times into his right ear, together with its ṛṣi and the rest. ॥87॥
6.13.88: Then, showing compassion, the best of gurus should teach the meaning of the praṇava, together with full knowledge of its six kinds of meaning. ॥88॥
6.13.89: He the disciple should prostrate to the guru on the ground like a staff in twelve ways. He should always remain dependent on him and should perform no other rite. ॥89॥
6.13.90: Then, by his command, the disciple should become devoted to the knowledge of Śiva in accordance with the meaning of the Vedānta, according to the distinction of Śiva with and without attributes. ॥90॥
6.13.91: Then the guru should have that very disciple perform the morning and other observances, preceded by the components beginning with hearing (śravaṇa), at the end of the japa. ॥91॥
6.13.92: And the worship, in that maṇḍala called Kailāsaprastara — the disciple should perform worship right there, by the method taught by Śiva. ॥92॥
6.13.93: If he is unable to worship the deity there daily, he should receive from the guru an auspicious crystal liṅga of the Lord, furnished with a pedestal. ॥93॥
6.13.94: He vows: Better for me the giving up of life, even the cutting off of my head, but I shall not eat without having worshipped the blessed three-eyed Lord. ॥94॥
6.13.95: Uttering this oath three times in the presence of the guru, the disciple, firm of mind and bearing devotion to Śiva, should take it. ॥95॥
6.13.96: From then on, with a mind ever zealous, he should worship Mahādeva daily with supreme devotion according to the method of the five enclosures (pañcāvaraṇa). ॥96॥
6.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
6.14.1: Vāmadeva said: O Lord, six-faced one, ocean of the nectar of complete knowledge, son of the lord of all the gods, destroyer of the distress of those who bow down to you, ॥1॥
6.14.2: What is this knowledge of the sixfold meaning that has been declared to grant what is desired? What are the six kinds of meaning there, and what is that knowledge, O Lord? ॥2॥
6.14.3: And who is the one it sets forth, and what is the fruit of knowing it? Explain all this, everything that I have asked, O Guha. ॥3॥
6.14.4: Not knowing this meaning, deluded by the teachings meant for bound souls (paśu-śāstra), I am even now confused by Śiva's māyā, O Mahāsena. ॥4॥
6.14.5: So that I, having drunk the elixir of the nectar of knowledge of Śiva's pair of feet, may become free from delusion— ॥5॥
6.14.6: —in that way, looking upon me for a long time with a glance moist with the nectar of compassion, grace should be shown to me, who have taken refuge at your glorious lotus-feet. ॥6॥
6.14.7: Having heard these words spoken by the lord of sages, the all-pervading one who holds the power of knowledge spoke words that cause great terror to other doctrines. ॥7॥
6.14.8: Subrahmaṇya said: Listen, O tiger among sages, to what you have asked with reverence: the knowledge of the Great Lord in terms of the collective and the individual. ॥8॥
6.14.9: That knowledge, which consists in understanding the meaning of the praṇava, I shall explain in detail through understanding the unity of the six kinds of meaning, O you of good vows. ॥9॥
6.14.10: The first meaning is the form of the mantra; the second is what is conceived through the mantra the yantra; the third meaning is the deity; after that comes the meaning as the manifest world— ॥10॥
6.14.11: —that is the fourth; the fifth meaning reveals the form of the guru; the sixth meaning is the form of the disciple's self. These are proclaimed as the six kinds of meaning. ॥11॥
6.14.12: Among these, I shall tell you the nature of the mantra, O best of sages, by merely knowing which a man becomes a great knower. ॥12॥
6.14.13: The first vowel a, the fifth u, and after that the last of the fifth consonant group, m, together with bindu and nāda—these five letters are declared by the Vedas, and not otherwise. ॥13॥
6.14.14: Their combined form is indeed declared to be the beginning of the Veda Om. Nāda is the aggregate of all; the group of four accompanied by bindu— ॥14॥
6.14.15: —is established in individual form in the praṇava that denotes Śiva. Now hear the yantra form, O wise one: that indeed is the Śiva-liṅga. ॥15॥
6.14.16: At the very bottom one should draw the pedestal; above it the first vowel a; above that the letter u; and above that the last of the pa-group m. ॥16॥
6.14.17: One should draw the bindu on its top and the nāda above that. When the yantra is complete, every desire is fulfilled. ॥17॥
6.14.18: Having thus drawn the yantra, one should encircle it with nine praṇavas; and by the nāda arising from it one should know it as ending in nāda. ॥18॥
6.14.19: I shall explain the meaning as deity, which is hidden everywhere, O sage, out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, just as Śaṅkara spoke it. ॥19॥
6.14.20: Beginning with sadyojātaṃ prapadyāmi and ending with sadāśivom, the Śruti has thus declared the tāra, the Praṇava, as denoting the five Brahmans. ॥20॥
6.14.21: The five subtle deities having the form of Brahman are to be known; these very ones are amplified as the embodied forms of Śiva too. ॥21॥
6.14.22: The mantra that denotes Śiva also denotes Śiva's form, since there is no absolute difference between the form and the one who has the form. ॥22॥
6.14.23: Śiva's body was described earlier, beginning with the words endowed with the crown of Īśāna; now hear about the five faces. ॥23॥
6.14.24: Beginning with the fifth, in order starting with Sadyojāta and ending with the upper one, Īśāna, the group of five faces is declared. ॥24॥
6.14.25: The fourfold Brahman-form, beginning with Puruṣa and ending with Sadyojāta, stands in the position of the fourfold emanation (catur-vyūha) of the god Īśāna himself. ॥25॥
6.14.26: Īśāna, renowned as Brahman, is the aggregate of the five Brahmans; and the four beginning with Puruṣa and ending with Sadyojāta are its individual forms, O sage. ॥26॥
6.14.27: This circle, consisting of grace, is the cause of the five purposes; it is of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, subtle, changeless and free from affliction. ॥27॥
6.14.28: Grace too is twofold: one pertains to concealment and the like; the other is that by which the Lord grants souls higher and lower liberation. ॥28॥
6.14.29: This pair of functions is declared to belong to Sadāśiva alone; and within grace too lies the Lord's set of five functions, creation and the rest. ॥29॥
6.14.30: There too, O sage, the deities beginning with Sadyojāta are proclaimed; those five, of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, always bestow welfare. ॥30॥
6.14.31: The circle of grace, consisting of the kalā beyond peace (śāntyatītā) and presided over by Sadāśiva, is called the supreme state. ॥31॥
6.14.32: This very state is to be attained by ascetics of purified selves, worshippers of Sadāśiva, whose minds are devoted to the praṇava. ॥32॥
6.14.33: Having attained this very state, the lords of sages, after enjoying very abundant pleasures together with him, the god in the form of Brahman, ॥33॥
6.14.34: at the occurrence of the great dissolution attain equality with Śiva; and those people never fall again anywhere into the ocean of saṃsāra. ॥34॥
6.14.35: They are in the Brahma-world—so the eternal Śruti says. And this indeed is the aggregate of Śiva's sovereignty as well. ॥35॥
6.14.36: Endowed with all sovereignty—so says the Atharva-śikhā; and they declare that the bestowing of all sovereignty belongs to him alone. ॥36॥
6.14.37: No state higher than the state of Camaka exists. The world is indeed seen as the unfolding of the expansion of the five Brahmans. ॥37॥
6.14.38: Thus the kalās beginning with Nivṛtti are held to have arisen from the Brahmans; they have the nature of the subtle elements and are renowned as causes. ॥38॥
6.14.39: That which exists in fivefold form within this world of gross nature, O you of good vows, is held to be the group of five Brahmans. ॥39॥
6.14.40: The pentad of Puruṣa, ear and speech, sound and space is pervaded by Brahman in the form of Īśāna, O best of sages. ॥40॥
6.14.41: The pentad of Prakṛti, skin and hand, touch and air is pervaded by Brahman in the form of Puruṣa, O lord of sages. ॥41॥
6.14.42: Ego (ahaṅkāra), the eye, the foot, form, and fire: this splendid group of five is pervaded by the Aghora-Brahman. ॥42॥
6.14.43: Intellect (buddhi), the tongue, the anus, taste, and water: this group of five is always pervaded by the Vāmadeva-Brahman. ॥43॥
6.14.44: Mind, the nose, the generative organ, smell, and earth: this group of five is pervaded by the Sadyojāta-Brahman. Thus the world consists of the five Brahmans. ॥44॥
6.14.45: The Praṇava, which denotes Śiva, is taught in the form of a yantra: it is the aggregate of the five letters, together with the group of four beginning with the bindu. ॥45॥
6.14.46: By the path taught by Śiva one should contemplate the Praṇava in the form of a yantra—the supreme king of mantras, whose form is Śiva. ॥46॥
6.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The description of the Praṇava as the form of Śiva, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
6.15.1: Īśvara said: Next I shall explain the excellent course of creation of the group of four beginning with Maheśa, as it arises from Sadāśiva, O fair-faced one. ॥1॥
6.15.2: Sadāśiva is the collective whole, the Lord, ruler of ether. The tetrad beginning with Maheśa is that very Sadāśiva having become individuated. ॥2॥
6.15.3: From a thousandth portion of Sadāśiva arose Maheśa; and since he has the form of Tatpuruṣa and is endless, he is the lord of air. ॥3॥
6.15.4: He is joined on his left with the Māyā-śakti, is with parts (sakala), and predominant in action. The tetrad beginning with Īśvara is his individuated form. ॥4॥
6.15.5: Īśa, then Viśveśvara, after that Parameśa, and next Sarveśvara — this is the excellent wheel of concealment (tirodhā). ॥5॥
6.15.6: Concealment is divided in two: one pertains to Rudra and the others; the other operates through embodiment for the continuing line of the class of bound souls (paśu), ॥6॥
6.15.7: intent on making them delight in enjoyments, lasting until the moment of the equipoise of karma. When karma is balanced, that same all-pervading one becomes full of grace. ॥7॥
6.15.8: There, the deities proclaimed with Sarveśvara as chief are directly of the nature of the supreme Brahman, free from distinctions and free from affliction. ॥8॥
6.15.9: The wheel consisting of concealment is made of the Śānti-kalā; presided over by Maheśvara, this abode is unsurpassed. ॥9॥
6.15.10: This very abode is to be attained by those who serve Maheśa's feet; for the Māheśvaras it grants liberation through the stages beginning with sālokya. ॥10॥
6.15.11: From a thousandth portion of Maheśvara was born the form of Rudra; he has the shape of the Aghora face and is ruler of the principle of fire (tejas). ॥11॥
6.15.12: Joined on his left with the Gaurī-śakti, the Lord is the destroyer of all. His individuated form is the tetrad beginning with Śiva. ॥12॥
6.15.13: Śiva, Hara, Mṛḍa and Bhava — this is known as the wondrous wheel called dissolution, greatly divine and supreme indeed, O lord of sages. ॥13॥
6.15.14: That dissolution is declared threefold by the wise, by the division beginning with the daily: the daily one is called the deep sleep of beings; the occasional one is considered to be that of Vidhi (Brahmā's night). ॥14॥
6.15.15: And his (Brahmā's) own dissolution is the great one — so the Veda shows. For beings exhausted by the sufferings of birth and the like, who have long dwelt in embodiment, ॥15॥
6.15.16: for their rest, O best of sages, and for the ripening of their karmas, dissolution was devised threefold by Rudra of immeasurable splendour. ॥16॥
6.15.17: This triad is declared to be among Rudra's own functions; yet even in dissolution the all-pervading Lord has the fivefold functions beginning with creation. ॥17॥
6.15.18: O sage, there the deities beginning with Bhava are proclaimed; they are of the nature of the supreme Brahman and bestow grace on the worlds. ॥18॥
6.15.19: This wheel called dissolution is made of the Vidyā-kalā; presided over by Rudra, this abode is free from affliction. ॥19॥
6.15.20: This very abode is to be attained by those who long to worship Rudra; for the Rudra-devotees it grants sāyujya (union) through the sequence of sālokya, O sage. ॥20॥
6.15.21: From a thousandth portion of the form of Rudra came the birth of Viṣṇu; he is the soul of the Vāmadeva wheel and the sole leader of the water principle. ॥21॥
6.15.22: Joined on his left with the Ramā-śakti, the great one is protector of all; four-armed, lotus-eyed, dark, bearing the conch and other emblems. ॥22॥
6.15.23: The group of four beginning with Vāsudeva is his individuated form; it grants liberation to the Vaiṣṇavas devoted to worship. ॥23॥
6.15.24: Vāsudeva, Aniruddha, then the supreme Saṅkarṣaṇa, and Pradyumna — thus is the renowned unsurpassed wheel of preservation. ॥24॥
6.15.25: Preservation is the protection of the created world together with its creator, until the end of the experiencing of the commenced (prārabdha) karma of beings who enjoy its fruits. ॥25॥
6.15.26: This function is declared to belong to Viṣṇu, the ordainer of protection; yet even in preservation the Lord has the fivefold functions beginning with creation. ॥26॥
6.15.27: There the deities headed by Pradyumna are proclaimed; they are free from distinctions, free from fear, and ever bestow the bliss of the liberated. ॥27॥
6.15.28: O Brahman, this wheel of preservation, excellent, has the form of the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā; presided over by Janārdana, it is called the supreme abode. ॥28॥
6.15.29: This very abode is to be attained by those who serve Viṣṇu's lotus feet; for the Vaiṣṇavas this wheel grants the states beginning with sālokya. ॥29॥
6.15.30: From a thousandth portion of Viṣṇu arose the Grandsire (Brahmā), who is the soul of the Sadyojāta face and leader of the earth principle. ॥30॥
6.15.31: Accompanied on his left by the goddess of speech, he is the creator and lord of the world, four-faced, red in colour, having the nature of rajas. ॥31॥
6.15.32: His individuated form is the tetrad beginning with Hiraṇyagarbha: Hiraṇyagarbha, then Virāṭ, Puruṣa, and Kāla. ॥32॥
6.15.33: This wheel of creation is served by the seers, the sons of Brahmā and others; O Brahman, it grants all desires and aims and bestows the happiness of family. ॥33॥
6.15.34: Creation, however, is bringing out this withdrawn soul, lying in Prakṛti, outward for the experience of karma, together with the means, the limbs, and the fruits, ॥34॥
6.15.35: and joining it with them — this function those who know the act of world-creation understand as the Grandsire's, extending throughout the happy array of creation. ॥35॥
6.15.36: Even in world-creation, O sage, the Lord has the fivefold functions. There the deities, Kāla and the others, are proclaimed. ॥36॥
6.15.37: This wheel of creation is declared by the wise to have the form of the Nivṛtti-kalā; presided over by the Grandsire, this abode is indeed beautiful. ॥37॥
6.15.38: This very abode is to be attained by men whose minds are offered to Brahmā; for the Paitāmahas (Brahmā's devotees) it grants liberation beginning with sālokya. ॥38॥
6.15.39: In this group of four wheels too the Praṇava is present; in the order beginning with Maheśa, it is their designator by secondary signification. ॥39॥
6.15.40: This, indeed, is the wheel of the world, whose glory is renowned in the Śruti; the Śruti praises it as the five-spoked wheel, O sage. ॥40॥
6.15.41: The wheel of the world, which is the unfolding of Śambhu's power, is one alone; having five members—creation and the rest—it is called five-spoked. ॥41॥
6.15.42: Because it revolves all around with uninterrupted dissolution and arising, like the whirling of a firebrand-circle, therefore it is called a wheel. ॥42॥
6.15.43: Because of the vast production of creation and the rest, it appears as vast—this wheel of the golden god Śambhu of immeasurable splendour. ॥43॥
6.15.44: This wheel, the effect of his power, rests on the golden light. It is enveloped by water; the water is enveloped by fire. ॥44॥
6.15.45: Fire is enveloped by wind, and the wind by space—that great one; likewise space by the bhūtādi (elemental ego), and the bhūtādi is enveloped by the Mahat. ॥45॥
6.15.46: Likewise the Mahat is enveloped by the Unmanifest. Thus, O best of sages, it has been declared by believing teachers to be the Cosmic Egg (brahmāṇḍa). ॥46॥
6.15.47: Seven sheaths are spoken of for the protection of this universe. The water is ordained to exceed the wheel tenfold. ॥47॥
6.15.48: And so, each one above the other, each is tenfold greater; that, O leader of sages, is to be understood by the wise as the Cosmic Egg. ॥48॥
6.15.49: Accepting this meaning, because the water lies near the wheel, the Veda itself declares, in the midst of the water. ॥49॥
6.15.50: Through grace, concealment, destruction, maintenance and creation, Śiva alone, united with Śakti, ceaselessly performs his play. ॥50॥
6.15.51: What use is saying much here, O sage? I tell you the essence: it is certain that all this is Śiva alone, the possessor of Śakti. ॥51॥
6.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The description of the forms for worship, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥15॥
6.16.1: Sūta said: Having heard the meaning of the Veda taught by the guru, the foremost of sages respectfully asked about what remained doubtful concerning the Supreme Self. ॥1॥
6.16.2: Vāmadeva said: O Lord, bearer of the power of knowledge, whose form is supreme bliss, the nectar of the meaning of the Praṇava, flowing from your blessed lotus-mouth, has been drunk by me. ॥2॥
6.16.3: I have become firm in understanding, and my doubt is gone. O Mahāsena, I ask you something else; listen, O Lord. ॥3॥
6.16.4: The existence of the world, whose forms range from Sadāśiva down to the worm, is seen everywhere in the form of female and male; there is no doubt of this. ॥4॥
6.16.5: The eternal cause of the world that has such a form — is it of female form, or is it male, or neuter? ॥5॥
6.16.6: Or is it mixed, or something else? No decision has arisen on this. The learned, bewildered by the scriptures, dispute here in many ways. ॥6॥
6.16.7: The Śrutis that ordain the creation of the world, together with the world itself, the gods beginning with Viṣṇu and Brahmā, and the Siddhas indeed do not know this. ॥7॥
6.16.8: Explain this, and something else as well, so that they may arrive at agreement. The usage I know, I do, is commonly seen. ॥8॥
6.16.9: That usage is indeed established in all beings; no one disputes it. But does it arise from the body, senses, mind, intellect and ego of all — ॥9॥
6.16.10: or is it the very form of the Self? Here too there is great doubt. These two indeed are a wondrous ground of dispute for everyone. ॥10॥
6.16.11: Uprooting the poison-tree called doubt, born of ignorance, so that my mind may become the soil for the great wish-fulfilling tree of Śiva-nondualism — ॥11॥
6.16.12: — so that my mind may become so, O god, I am to be instructed through your compassion. By your grace, O lord of gods, I shall become one of firm knowledge. ॥12॥
6.16.13: Sūta said: Having heard the words thus asked by the sage, steeped in Vedānta, the Lord, with a slightly smiling face, spoke this secret. ॥13॥
6.16.14: Subrahmaṇya said: O sage Vāmadeva, this very secret was expounded by Śiva to the Mother Goddess, while I too was listening. ॥14॥
6.16.15: Having then drunk her breast-milk, I was satisfied again and again; I heard it attentively, and it was ascertained and reflected upon by me. ॥15॥
6.16.16: Out of compassion I tell it to you, O Vāmadeva, great sage. Listen now, dear son, to this great and supreme secret. ॥16॥
6.16.17: Beginning from the view that karma exists and from the tattvas, the discourse of the śāstras is very extensive; O sage, what gives knowledge should be heard by the wise according to discernment. ॥17॥
6.16.18: Among the disciples you have taught, who indeed is equal to you? Those lowly ones still wander even today among the systems of Kapila and others. ॥18॥
6.16.19: Devoted to reviling Śiva, they were cursed long ago by six sages. Their talk should not be heard, since they speak contrary to the truth. ॥19॥
6.16.20: Here there is no need for scope even for applying a five-membered inference; yet, from the sight of smoke, ॥20॥
6.16.21: they declare that the mountain possesses fire; here too, O you of good vows, it rests on the perception of the visible world. Therefore — ॥21॥
6.16.22: — the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Self, is to be known; there is no doubt. The universe consisting of female and male forms is seen by direct perception itself. ॥22॥
6.16.23: The body has the form of six sheaths; among them the first three are born of the mother's portion, and the others of the father's portion — so says the Śruti. ॥23॥
6.16.24: Thus people know the female-male nature in all bodies; and the wise, O sage, know the female-male nature in the Supreme Self as well. ॥24॥
6.16.25: The Śruti declares Brahman to have the nature of existence-consciousness-bliss. The word sat, which removes non-existence, is said to be the Self. ॥25॥
6.16.26: The removal of insentience is effected by the word cit. The word sat, which occurs in all three genders, should here be taken as masculine. ॥26॥
6.16.27: It denotes light; clearly, sat means light. The word cit, a synonym of the word jñāna (knowledge), has taken the feminine gender. ॥27॥
6.16.28: Light and consciousness, as a couple, have become the cause of the world. Likewise, in the Self that is existence-consciousness, which has become the cause of the world, ॥28॥
6.16.29: the notion Śiva and Śakti is established in one single place. Even light has impurity, owing to oil, wick and the like; ॥29॥
6.16.30: impurity and inauspiciousness are seen in the fire of the funeral pyre and the like. Thus, as the remover of these, auspiciousness (Śivatva) is enjoined by the Śruti. ॥30॥
6.16.31: The power of consciousness resting in the individual soul always has weakness; to remove that, here, Śakti-hood is eternal. ॥31॥
6.16.32: The usage strong and powerful is constantly seen in the world and in the Veda, O Vāmadeva, great sage. ॥32॥
6.16.33: Thus Śiva-hood and Śakti-hood are shown in the Supreme Self; from the union of Śiva and Śakti, bliss constantly arises. ॥33॥
6.16.34: Therefore, O sage, aiming at that bliss, sages whose sins were destroyed fixed their minds on Śiva and attained Śiva, the untroubled. ॥34॥
6.16.35: Thus the all-pervading selfhood of those two is sung in the Upaniṣads as Brahman, by the word brahman, which falls within the sense of the root bṛṃh (to expand). ॥35॥
6.16.36: Expanding and greatness reside in the form called Śambhu, consisting of the five Brahmans; the manifestation of the universe therein is denoted by the word brahman. ॥36॥
6.16.37: Out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, I shall tell of the origin of the Praṇava from the Haṃsa mantra in reverse order; listen attentively. ॥37॥
6.16.38: By dropping the consonants s and h, there remains only Om, the gross designator of the Supreme Self. ॥38॥
6.16.39: It should be known as the great mantra by sages who see the truth. Within it is the subtle great mantra; I shall tell you its extraction. ॥39॥
6.16.40: In the first vowel, in the one of the form three-times-five (the fifteenth), and in the sixteenth vowel — in these three — when it is joined with s at the beginning, the great mantra arises. ॥40॥
6.16.41: The reverse of haṃsa would be so'ham; the meaning of the letter sa is held to be Śiva. The one consisting of Śakti is what the great mantra denotes; this is the conclusion. ॥41॥
6.16.42: But at the time of the guru's instruction, it means, I am he, Śiva consisting of Śakti; thus the great mantra should refer to the individual soul. Then the bound soul (paśu), ॥42॥
6.16.43: consisting of Śakti and being a portion of Śiva, through oneness with Śiva comes to share equality with Śiva. In the Brahman-statement prajñānam brahma, the meaning of prajñāna is seen. ॥43॥
6.16.44: The word prajñāna is a synonym of consciousness (caitanya); there is no doubt. O sage, the Śiva-sūtra, Consciousness is the Self, was set forth. ॥44॥
6.16.45: Consciousness means the freedom over the universe consisting of all knowledge and action; he whose own nature is that is declared to be the Self. ॥45॥
6.16.46: I have given the commentary (vārttika) on the Śiva-sūtras beginning thus. Knowledge is bondage is the Lord's second sūtra. ॥46॥
6.16.47: Knowledge here is that of the self consisting of limited knowledge and action; thus by the first word the Lord stated the characteristic of the class of bound souls. ॥47॥
6.16.48: This pair, knowledge and action, is the first stirring (spanda) of the Supreme Śakti. This very Supreme Śakti the followers of the Śvetāśvatara branch ॥48॥
6.16.49: joyfully praised as natural to him is the action of knowledge and strength. Indeed they know Śambhu's threefold vision as having the form of knowledge, action and will. ॥49॥
6.16.50: This triad, being located within the mind, the bound soul, having entered the sphere of sense-knowledge, always knows and acts through it. ॥50॥
6.16.51: Therefore it is settled that this is the very form of the Self. I shall now expound the meaning of the manifest world, showing its oneness with the Praṇava. ॥51॥
6.16.52: The eternal Śruti says, Om is all this. Beginning with From that Self, verily, the creation of the world is declared. ॥52॥
6.16.53: Out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, I shall tell the purport of that Śruti, unfolded for the sake of discernment; let this be heard. ॥53॥
6.16.54: The union of Śiva and Śakti is settled to be the Supreme Self. From the Supreme Śakti arose Cit-śakti, born of it; ॥54॥
6.16.55: from that was born Ānanda-śakti; from that arose Icchā-śakti; from that was born Jñāna-śakti; and Kriyā-śakti is the fifth. From these alone, O sage, arose the kalās beginning with Nivṛtti. ॥55॥
6.16.56: Nāda and Bindu are declared to have arisen from Cit and Ānanda. From Icchā-śakti comes the letter ma, and from Jñāna-śakti the fifth ॥56॥
6.16.57: vowel u; and the letter a is born of Kriyā-śakti, O lord of sages. Thus the origin of the Praṇava has been told; now hear the origin of the five Brahmans. ॥57॥
6.16.58: From Śiva arose Īśāna; from that the origin of Tatpuruṣa; then Aghora; then Vāmadeva; and then the origin of Sadyojāta. ॥58॥
6.16.59: From this mātṛkā arose the thirty-eight mātṛs (kalās). From Īśāna was born the kalā called Śāntyatītā; then from Tatpuruṣa arises the Śānti kalā; Vidyā is born of Aghora; ॥59॥
6.16.60: Pratiṣṭhā and Nivṛtti are held to arise from Vāma and Sadyojāta. From Īśa, headed by Cit-śakti, comes the fivefold pair of the all-pervading Lord. ॥60॥
6.16.61: This pentad is regarded as the cause of the functions beginning with grace, by wise sages who know it and reveal the highest truth. ॥61॥
6.16.62: In this pentad, which has become paired through the relation of denoted and denoter and has the nature of kalās and letters, the pentad of elements ॥62॥
6.16.63: came forth in order beginning with space, O best of sages, starting from the first pair up to the fifth, of which each element is known to consist. ॥63॥
6.16.64: Space has sound as its sole quality; air has the qualities of sound and touch; fire is said to be predominant in the qualities of sound, touch and form. ॥64॥
6.16.65: Water is held to have the qualities of sound, touch, form and taste; earth is held to be rich in sound, touch, form, taste and smell. ॥65॥
6.16.66: This very order is declared as the pervasiveness of the elements; their being pervaded is in reverse, in the order beginning with smell. ॥66॥
6.16.67: This manifest world, consisting of the five elements, is declared to be Virāṭ, the self of the totality of all, and clearly the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa). ॥67॥
6.16.68: Beginning from the earth-principle up to the Śiva-principle in order, the individual soul, merging into the mass of principles, is itself dissolved. ॥68॥
6.16.69: Again at creation, together with Śakti, he emerges through Śakti and remains happily in the form of the gross world until dissolution. ॥69॥
6.16.70: The first stirring of the great Lord, when he is intent on creating the world by his own will, is called the Śiva-principle. ॥70॥
6.16.71: This very will is the Śakti-principle, since it accompanies all functions. In the pair of knowledge- and action-powers, when knowledge predominates, it is Sadāśiva. ॥71॥
6.16.72: Know, O lord of sages, that when action predominates it is the Maheśvara principle. The equality of the knowledge- and action-powers is held to be the pure principle of the nature of Vidyā. ॥72॥
6.16.73: The notion of difference with regard to entities which are his own limbs is the Māyā-principle. When Śiva, his own form preceded by supreme lordship ॥73॥
6.16.74: concealing by Māyā, becomes the perceiver of all objects, then he bears the name Puruṣa; the Śruti, having created it, he entered into it, arose about this. ॥74॥
6.16.75: This very one is the transmigrating bound soul, deluded by Māyā, devoid of the knowledge of Śiva, his mind bewildered by various actions. ॥75॥
6.16.76: Delusion arises only for this bound soul, who knows the world as not non-different from Śiva and himself as different from him; not for the Lord, ॥76॥
6.16.77: just as there is no illusion for the magician or the yogin. One whose lordship is made known by the guru becomes Śiva, a mass of consciousness. ॥77॥
6.16.78: Having the form of all-doership, of the nature of omniscience, having the form of fullness, of the nature of eternity and pervasiveness — ॥78॥
6.16.79: these are the five powers of Śiva, which shine forth in contracted form, ॥79॥
6.16.80: always appearing even in the form of contraction. For the bound soul they become kalā, vidyā, rāga, kāla and niyati; in the form of this pentad of principles, here that first is called kalā. ॥80॥
6.16.81: Kalā would be the cause of limited agency; that which is the sole means of limited knowing (tattva) is vidyā; and rāga is that which makes one attached to sense-objects. ॥81॥
6.16.82: Kāla (time), whose nature is to make manifest the appearances of existent and non-existent things, becoming the delimiter of sequence, is spoken of as past and so on. ॥82॥
6.16.83: The power of the all-pervading Lord that regulates thus: This is to be done by me, this is not—that is niyati; by its impulsion the bound soul (paśu) falls. ॥83॥
6.16.84: This very group of five, because it veils his true nature, is declared to be the five sheaths (pañca-kañcuka), and the inner instrument of bondage. ॥84॥
6.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The description of the principle of Śiva, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
6.17.1: Vāmadeva said: Earlier you said that the Puruṣa is situated below Niyati and above Prakṛti; how is it now stated otherwise— ॥1॥
6.17.2: that, his form contracted by Māyā, he is then below it, O Lord? This doubt of mine, O master, you should cut away in truth. ॥2॥
6.17.3: Śrī Subrahmaṇya said: This is the doctrine of non-dual Śaivism; it nowhere tolerates duality. Duality is perishable; the non-dual Brahman is supreme and imperishable. ॥3॥
6.17.4: Śiva is omniscient, the maker of all, the lord of all, beyond the guṇas; he is Brahman, the begetter of the three gods, whose form is being, consciousness and bliss. ॥4॥
6.17.5: That very god Śaṅkara, by his own will and his own Māyā, became the Puruṣa, being as if of contracted form. ॥5॥
6.17.6: Constituted as experiencer by the group of five beginning with Kalā, this Puruṣa, abiding in Prakṛti, enjoys the guṇas born of Prakṛti. ॥6॥
6.17.7: Thus the Puruṣa, standing within both positions, is not contradictory; contracting, he possesses the aggregate of his own forms such as knowledge. ॥7॥
6.17.8: The citta, to be effected by the guṇas sattva and the rest, and threefold as intellect and the rest—that was the Prakṛti-principle, owing to sattva and the others as cause. ॥8॥
6.17.9: The guṇas arising from Prakṛti are distinguished as sāttvika and the rest; from the guṇas arose the intellect, which determines things. ॥9॥
6.17.10: Then came the great ego, and from it the sense organs of knowledge were born; the form of the mind is that which conceives and doubts. ॥10॥
6.17.11: The organs of knowledge are ear, skin, eye, tongue and nose; sound, touch, form, taste and smell are their objects— ॥11॥
6.17.12: —declared as belonging to the organs of knowledge in order, beginning with the ear. Then from the vaikārika ego the subtle elements (tanmātras) arose in sequence. ॥12॥
6.17.13: These are called subtle by sages who see the truth. The organs of action, together with their functions, should be known: ॥13॥
6.17.14: O brahmin sage, speech, the two hands, the two feet, the anus and the genital; their actions are called speaking, grasping, going, excretion and pleasure. ॥14॥
6.17.15: From the bhūtādi ego the subtle elements arose in sequence; they are the subtle forms of sound and the rest—so is the established view. ॥15॥
6.17.16: And from them, O tiger among sages, the birth of space, air, fire, water and earth in order should be understood; this is called the five elements. ॥16॥
6.17.17: Giving room, conveying, cooking, cohesion and supporting are declared to be their functions. ॥17॥
6.17.18: Vāmadeva said: Earlier the creation of the elements was said to be from Kalā and the rest; how is it again stated otherwise, O Skanda? Great is my doubt here. ॥18॥
6.17.19: You said: The Ātma-principle is the letter A; Vidyā is U, beyond that; the Śiva-principle is M—let this be contemplated, O Vāmadeva. ॥19॥
6.17.20: Bindu and Nāda should both be known as conveying the meaning of all principles. Now hear, O sage, the deities residing there: ॥20॥
6.17.21: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Maheśvara and Sadāśiva—they are directly the forms of Śiva himself, renowned in the Veda. ॥21॥
6.17.22: So you said earlier; now it is said otherwise, that the elements arise from the subtle elements. Great is my doubt here. ॥22॥
6.17.23: Showing that compassion, O Skanda, you should cut away the doubt. Hearing these words of the sage, Kumāra replied. ॥23॥
6.17.24: Śrī Subrahmaṇya said: Beginning from the Vedic passage tasmād vā, in the order of the creation of the elements, O sage, hear them, O most wise one, attentively and with respect. ॥24॥
6.17.25: It is settled that the five elements were born from the Kalās; they, forming the gross world, are the body of the Lord of beings. ॥25॥
6.17.26: In the order of the emergence of principles, from the Śiva-principle down to earth, the elements are to be described in sequence as arising from the subtle elements, O sage. ॥26॥
6.17.27: The union of the subtle elements and the Kalās is the cause of the elements; know that there is no contradiction here, O best of knowers of Brahman. ॥27॥
6.17.28: In the universe, gross and subtle, the planets such as moon and sun, along with the constellations, came into being, and likewise other hosts of luminaries; ॥28॥
6.17.29: the deities Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa and others, the classes of beings, the guardians of the quarters such as Indra, the gods, the ancestors, the asuras, ॥29॥
6.17.30: rākṣasas, humans and other mobile beings, beasts, birds, insects, and the various kinds such as serpents, ॥30॥
6.17.31: trees, shrubs, creepers and herbs, the eight famed mountains, the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, and the oceans of great wealth— ॥31॥
6.17.32: whatever collection of things there is, all that is established here in Śiva; it should be reflected upon with right understanding, not as outside, O best of sages. ॥32॥
6.17.33: This universe, of female and male form, whose nature is Śiva and Śakti, should be worshipped by the wise like you, skilled in the knowledge of Śiva. ॥33॥
6.17.34: One should worship all as Brahman, and also, All indeed is Rudra—so says the Veda, O sage; therefore Sadāśiva is the self of the world. ॥34॥
6.17.35: Through the power of the placement of the thirty-eight Kalās and through non-dual contemplation, the guru whose self is cultivated as I am Sadāśiva alone is Śiva. ॥35॥
6.17.36: A true disciple who reflects thus becomes a guru; he is Śiva himself, whose self is the world, the deities, yantras and mantras—there is no doubt. ॥36॥
6.17.37: By the grace of the teacher, O brahmin, the disciple, all his bonds cut away and devoted to Śiva's state, surely becomes one with the guru. ॥37॥
6.17.38: Whatever thing exists, all of it—taken collectively or severally, according to the predominance of its guṇas—they declare to be the meaning of the Praṇava. ॥38॥
6.17.39: Free from faults such as passion, the essence of the Veda, spoken by Śiva—this non-dual knowledge dear to Śiva has been told to you by me with affection. ॥39॥
6.17.40: Whoever, puffed up with pride, considers this word of mine otherwise—be he a god, a dānava, a siddha, a gandharva, or even a human— ॥40॥
6.17.41: With this unequalled true power (śakti), which is like the fire of universal destruction to enemies, you would surely cut off the head of that wicked-souled one; there is no doubt. ॥41॥
6.17.42: You alone, O sage, are manifestly the foremost among the knowers of Śiva's non-duality; indeed, in teaching the knowledge of Śiva, you are the one who demonstrates Śiva's conduct. ॥42॥
6.17.43: By contact with the ash of your body, an impure great piśāca, his mass of sins cut away, attained through your grace the goal of the virtuous. ॥43॥
6.17.44: You are one whose glory is renowned throughout the three worlds by the name Śivayogī; by contact with your glance a bound soul (paśu) would become Paśupati. ॥44॥
