6.17.45: Your questioning of me about that is out of earnest care for the instruction of the world; the virtuous wander here for the sake of benefiting the world. ॥45॥
6.17.46: Therefore this supreme secret is established in you. You too, with faith, devotion and respect, teaching those devoted to the praṇava— ॥46॥
6.17.47: —having seated them all and united them with the Supreme Lord, make them adopt Śiva's conduct, together with sacred ash and rudrākṣa. ॥47॥
6.17.48: You are indeed Śiva, a follower of Śiva's conduct, through the non-dual state you have attained; wandering for the protection of the world, attain imperishable bliss. ॥48॥
6.17.49: Sūta said: Having heard this wondrous doctrine spoken by the six-faced one, grounded in Vedānta, the sage became humble in form, and bowing many times on the ground like a staff, attained the state of a bee roaming at his lotus feet. ॥49॥
6.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The account of creation, beginning with the teaching of the knowledge of non-duality with Śiva, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
6.18.1: Śaunaka said: Having heard that essence of Vedānta, a secret most wonderful, what did Vāmadeva then ask the son of Maheśvara? ॥1॥
6.18.2: Blessed is the yogī Vāmadeva, ever devoted to the knowledge of Śiva, through whose connection this divine, supremely purifying narrative arose. ॥2॥
6.18.3: Having heard these words of the sages, full of love, the wise Sūta, his mind attached to Śiva, being pleased, spoke to them. ॥3॥
6.18.4: Sūta said: Blessed are you, devotees of Mahādeva, benefactors of the world. Listen, all you sages, once more to the dialogue of those two. ॥4॥
6.18.5: Having heard the words of Maheśa's son, which destroy duality and give rise to non-dual knowledge, the great sage became satisfied. ॥5॥
6.18.6: Bowing to Kārtikeya, son of Śiva, and praising him in various ways, the great sage again humbly asked about the truth. ॥6॥
6.18.7: Vāmadeva said: O Lord, knower of all truths, O six-faced one, ocean of nectar, how does the status of guru arise for these renunciants whose selves are purified— ॥7॥
6.18.8: by whose power beings attain the accomplishment of enjoyment, liberation and the rest? Without a line of succession they have no authority to give instruction. ॥8॥
6.18.9: Likewise, how is the shaving rite, as a component, and such a bath performed? Please explain this, O master; you are able to cut away my doubt. ॥9॥
6.18.10: Having heard this, Kārtikeya, keeping Vāmadeva's words in mind and remembering Śiva and Śivā in his heart, began to explain. ॥10॥
6.18.11: Śrī Subrahmaṇya said: Out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, I shall declare the Yogapaṭṭa rite, through which guruhood arises—a great secret that grants liberation. ॥11॥
6.18.12: In the month of Vaiśākha, Śrāvaṇa, likewise Āśvayuja, Kārtika, Mārgaśīrṣa or Māgha, in the bright fortnight, on an auspicious day, ॥12॥
6.18.13: on the fifth lunar day or the full-moon day, having performed the morning rites and received permission from the guru, the disciple should bathe, with a controlled mind. ॥13॥
6.18.14: Having performed full bodily cleansing and wiped the body with a cloth, having tied on a doubled cord and put on two garments, ॥14॥
6.18.15: with feet washed, having sipped water twice, he should take ash and apply it with the Sadyojāta and other mantras, in the manner of full smearing. ॥15॥
6.18.16: Then, O sage, his hand held by the kindly guru, that disciple, with joined palms of his own two hands, facing east, ॥16॥
6.18.17: being thus seated, should remain in the well-decorated pavilion, on a pure, excellent seat of the guru, covered with cloth, deerskin and kuśa grass. ॥17॥
6.18.18: Then the preceptor, taking the conch together with its stand and purifying it with the Astra mantra, should kindly place it in front of him. ॥18॥
6.18.19: Having worshipped the conch with its stand with flowers and the like, he should pour into it good water purified with the Astra and Kavaca mantras. ॥19॥
6.18.20: Having filled it and worshipped it as before, following the order prescribed for the six limbs, he should again consecrate it seven times with the Praṇava. ॥20॥
6.18.21: Having worshipped it with fragrance, flowers and so on, and shown incense and lamp, having protected that conch with the Astra, he should then veil it with the Kavaca. ॥21॥
6.18.22: Then the preceptor should display the gestures called Dhenu and Śaṅkha. Again, placing the conch before himself on an excellent spot to the right, ॥22॥
6.18.23: he should make a beautiful, auspicious maṇḍala according to the procedure prescribed for the worship-arghya, and worship it with fragrant flowers and the like. ॥23॥
6.18.24: A pot with its stand, cleansed and pure, adorned with thread, fumigated with incense, set in place, and filled with pure scented water— ॥24॥
6.18.25: that pot, O lord of sages, he should smear with the five barks, the five leaves and the five clays, mixed with fragrant substance. ॥25॥
6.18.26: Then he should make that pot well adorned with cloth, mango leaves, tips of dūrvā grass, a coconut, flowers and other articles. ॥26॥
6.18.27: He should place the five gems in that pot, O lord of sages; or, in their absence, he should devoutly place gold. ॥27॥
6.18.28: The gem called sapphire, likewise the two gems ruby and gold, and coral and gomedaka (zircon)—this is known as the set of five gems. ॥28॥
6.18.29: Then the preceptor, uttering nṛmluska and then glūṃ at the end, should, kindly disposed, worship properly and lovingly according to the rule. ॥29॥
6.18.30: Beginning with the Ādhāraśakti, according to the procedure stated for worship, he should invoke the deity and worship him by way of the five enclosures (āvaraṇas). ॥30॥
6.18.31: Having offered rice-pudding, betel and the rest as before, and having completed the worship ending with the eight names, he should consecrate it the pot with mantras: ॥31॥
6.18.32: with the Praṇava one hundred and eight times, then with the five Brahma-mantras in order, from Sadyojāta up to Īśāna, and also with the Astra; then, protected again with the Kavaca, ॥32॥
6.18.33: having veiled it, and having devoutly shown incense and lamp, he should then properly display there the gestures called Dhenu and Yoni. ॥33॥
6.18.34: Then the preceptor, covering its top with darbha grass, should prepare a square in the north-eastern (Īśāna) quarter of the maṇḍala. ॥34॥
6.18.35: Having arranged a pleasing seat upon it according to rule, he should kindly seat the disciple, that novice, there. ॥35॥
6.18.36: Then, lifting the pot, preceded by the recitation of auspicious blessings (svastivācana), the guru should sprinkle the disciple on the head, moving clockwise. ॥36॥
6.18.37: First uttering the Praṇava seven times, then the five Brahma-mantras, at the end of the ablution he should encircle him with the water of the conch. ॥37॥
6.18.38: Then, having shown a beautiful lamp and wiped him with a cloth, he should make him wear a new cord, loincloth and two garments. ॥38॥
6.18.39: With feet washed and having sipped water twice, the guru, himself wearing ash, holding the novice's two hands with his own hands in the middle of the pavilion, ॥39॥
6.18.40: the guru, having duly smeared that ash on his limbs, should then lead him to the prepared seat and seat him comfortably. ॥40॥
6.18.41: To him the disciple who faces east and longs for knowledge of the principle of his own self, the guru, seated on his own seat, should say: Be of pure self. ॥41॥
6.18.42: And the guru, firmly established in the conviction, I am Śiva, the all-full, should properly enter samādhi for a muhūrta, with his mind withdrawn inward. ॥42॥
6.18.43: Afterwards, opening his eyes, with a favourable mind and undisturbed, he should look upon the pure disciple standing with folded hands. ॥43॥
6.18.44: Placing his own hand, smeared with sacred ash, on the disciple's head, he should clearly impart into his right ear: Haṃsaḥ so'ham. ॥44॥
6.18.45: There, the meaning of the first word aham is the one whose nature is Śakti; saḥ is Śiva himself. He alone am I; I am Śiva — thus contemplate your own self. ॥45॥
6.18.46: Having thus taught the essential meaning of ya (the relative who) with respect to the individual soul (aṇu), he should then carefully explain the meaning and purport of the intermediate statements. ॥46॥
6.18.47: He should say clearly: I shall tell you the statements, O Brahman; listen with an attentive mind, and hold them firmly in your heart. ॥47॥
6.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The rite of making a disciple, in the procedure of saṃnyāsa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
6.19.0: Subrahmaṇya said: Now the great sayings: (1) Consciousness is Brahman. (2) I am Brahman. (3) That you are. (4) This Self is Brahman. (5) All this is to be pervaded by the Lord. (6) I am prāṇa. (7) The Self is consciousness. (8) What is here, that is there; what is there, that is here too. (9) That is other than the known, and also beyond the unknown. (10) This is our Self, the inner controller, the immortal. (11) He who is in the person and he who is in the sun, he is one. (12) I am the supreme Brahman, beyond the higher and the lower, higher than the highest. (13) Through the Vedas, the śāstras and the guru, it is known as itself marked by bliss. (14) The Brahman abiding in all beings, that indeed am I; there is no doubt. (15) I am the prāṇa of the tattva; I am the prāṇa of earth. (16) I am the prāṇa of the waters, and I am the prāṇa of fire. (17) I am the prāṇa of air; I am the prāṇa of ether. (18) I am the prāṇa of the three guṇas. (19) I am all, I am the self of all, the one in saṃsāra; whatever has been, whatever will be, whatever is present, because I am the self of all, I am without a second. (20) All this indeed is Brahman. (21) I am all, I am liberated. (22) He who is that one, I am he; haṃsa: I am he.
6.19.1: The meaning of the saying Consciousness is Brahman has already been explained before. What the word aham (I) refers to is the Supreme Lord, whose self is Śakti. ॥1॥
6.19.2: The letter a, foremost of all letters, is light, the supreme Śiva. The letter ha has the form of space; it is declared to be of the nature of Śakti. ॥2॥
6.19.3: From the union of Śiva and Śakti arises bliss, ever manifest. The word Brahman denotes the all-selfhood of Śiva and Śakti; this is clear. ॥3॥
6.19.4: That was taught earlier; one should contemplate, I am he. In tat tvam, the meaning of the word tat has been explained. ॥4॥
6.19.5: Otherwise, in so 'ham there would be a contemplation of a contrary meaning. The word aham is masculine, while tat would be neuter; thus, owing to their mutual contradiction, there could be no grammatical connection between the two. ॥5॥
6.19.6: And otherwise the cause of the world, which has the form of female and male, would be something different. Thus sa tvam asi (he you are) is the contemplation of the meaning of the teaching. ॥6॥
6.19.7: And in the saying ayam ātmā, the pair of words is masculine in form. Because it is to be protected by the Lord (īśa), this world is īśāvāsya. ॥7॥
6.19.8: One should contemplate prajñānātmā and, what is here, that is there. He who is here is that very one — so it is stated here by learned adherents of the established doctrine. ॥8॥
6.19.9: And in the saying stated above, he who is there abides here; thus, as before, the meaning is the Puruṣa, according to the view of the wise. ॥9॥
6.19.10: That is other than the known, and also than the unknown — in this saying too there arises a notion of reversal even of the result. ॥10॥
6.19.11: How that may be, just so I shall explain here; listen, O sage. The word aviditāt is to be taken as before, like viditāt; ॥11॥
6.19.12: it would be employed thus: that is other than the known, and likewise beyond the unknown. It is certain that what is other would not serve for attainment in any other sense. ॥12॥
6.19.13: This is your Self, the inner controller, who is immortal and Śiva himself; the Śambhu who is in the person and who abides in the sun. ॥13॥
6.19.14: He and that one suggest separateness; yet he is not one place alone — he is declared to be all. The meaning here involves two limiting adjuncts; it is spoken thus figuratively. ॥14॥
6.19.15: The Śrutis indeed call that Lord Śambhu golden; the phrase to the golden-armed is an indication of all his limbs. ॥15॥
6.19.16: Otherwise his lordship over that would not hold; this is to be understood carefully. He who is within — so Śambhu, Śiva, is heard of in the Chāndogya. ॥16॥
6.19.17: Having a golden beard, and likewise golden hair; from the nails to the tips of the hair, he is golden everywhere. ॥17॥
6.19.18: I am the supreme Brahman, beyond higher and lower, higher than the highest — I shall tell the purport of this saying; listen to this. ॥18॥
6.19.19: The referent of the word aham is declared to be Śiva, whose self is Śakti. I am he alone — such is certainly the construal of the meaning of the saying. ॥19॥
6.19.20: He, most excellent of all and the self of all, is declared to be the supreme Brahman. Para, apara, and parātpara — thus it is threefold. ॥20॥
6.19.21: Rudra, Brahmā and Viṣṇu are so declared by Śruti itself, not otherwise; and the supreme God beyond them is indicated by the word para. ॥21॥
6.19.22: Through the force of repeated study of the sayings of the Vedas, śāstras and gurus, Śambhu, full of perfect bliss, becomes manifest in the heart of the disciple. ॥22॥
6.19.23: Śambhu abides in all beings; he indeed am I, there is no doubt. I am the prāṇa of the whole multitude of tattvas; I am Śiva. ॥23॥
6.19.24: Having said this, Śiva spoke again of being the prāṇa of the three tattvas. In the words I am prāṇa, O sage, from the inclusion of everything from earth up to the guṇas, ॥24॥
6.19.25: understand that all the ātma-tattvas are included. And again, the inclusion of all refers to the vidyā-tattva and the Śiva-tattva. ॥25॥
6.19.26: And of these two tattvas I am the prāṇas; I am all, indeed the self of all. And because I am the inner controller of the jīva, I am always its very life. ॥26॥
6.19.27: Whatever has been, whatever is to be, whatever will be — all of it; because it consists of me, I am all. All indeed is Rudra — ॥27॥
6.19.28: so the Śruti says, O sage, for it issued directly from Śiva's mouth. He is the self of all because of his eternal association with these supreme qualities. ॥28॥
6.19.29: Since there is no supreme self other than myself, I alone am without a second. The meaning of the saying All this indeed is Brahman was stated earlier. ॥29॥
6.19.30: I am full, being of the nature of pure being; I alone am eternally liberated. The paśus (bound souls), through my grace, are liberated, having taken refuge in my state. ॥30॥
6.19.31: That Śambhu who is the self of all — he am I; haṃsa — I am Śiva. Such indeed, O Vāmadeva, is the meaning of all the sayings, as declared by Śiva. ॥31॥
6.19.32: Thus the guru should carefully teach the disciple the meaning taught through the sayings of the Lord and of Śruti, which directly grants men oneness with Śiva. ॥32॥
6.19.33: Taking a conch together with its stand, purifying it with ash by means of the astra-mantra, and placing it before him on a worshipped square, ॥33॥
6.19.34: having worshipped the astra with Om using perfumes and the rest, adorned with cloth, filling it with scented water and worshipping it with the mantra Om, ॥34॥
6.19.35: then consecrating it again sevenfold with the praṇava he says: Whoever makes even the slightest distinction becomes subject to great fear — ॥35॥
6.19.36: thus speaks the true principle of Śruti; be firm of soul and free of fear. Having thus addressed the disciple himself, meditating on the God, he should worship. ॥36॥
6.19.37: Having worshipped the disciple's seat by the method of the six upliftings, and having conceived it as the seat of Śiva, he should form the image of Śiva upon it. ॥37॥
6.19.38: Placing the five Brahman-mantras from the head down to the feet, and also the kalās of the praṇava, according to the divisions of head, face and kalās, ॥38॥
6.19.39: the thirty-eight in the form of mantras, on the disciple's body and then on the head; having invoked Śiva, he should display the mudrās of establishing. ॥39॥
6.19.40: Then, having placed the limbs of the mantra in order, beginning with sarvajña (the omniscient), he should arrange the sixteen services of worship, starting with the offering of a seat. ॥40॥
6.19.41: Having offered rice cooked in milk as the food-offering with Om and the word for Agni's wife (svāhā), he should offer in order water for rinsing the mouth, sipping water, arghya and the rest, and incense, lamp and the rest. ॥41॥
6.19.42: Having worshipped Śiva with the eight names, he should then recite, together with brāhmaṇas who have mastered the Vedas, the passages brahmavid āpnoti and bhṛgur vai vāruṇiḥ. ॥42॥
6.19.43: He should recite starting from yo devānām up to yaḥ paraḥ sa maheśvaraḥ. Then, in front of him, a garland made of kahlāra lilies and other flowers — ॥43॥
6.19.44: — taking up the garland and standing up, he should softly recite the Siddhi-skandha in the five-faced form of the text within the scripture composed by Śrī Virūpākṣa, ॥44॥
6.19.45: from khyātiḥ up to pūrṇo'ham (I am full); then the preceptor, with a favourable mind, should place the garland on the neck of that disciple. ॥45॥
6.19.46: Then he should have a tilaka mark made with sandal paste, and again the anointing of all the limbs, in keeping with his own tradition, according to rule. ॥46॥
6.19.47: Then the preceptor, with affection, should give him a name bearing the title Śrīpāda, an umbrella and sandals, and the right of performing the dūrvā rites, ॥47॥
6.19.48: and the office of expounder, the ritual duties and so on, and the acceptance of the guru's seat — the guru, having bestowed these as grace upon that disciple who has the form of Śiva, ॥48॥
6.19.49: and having told him, Always remain established in samādhi, thinking, I am Śiva, should then himself make a prostration to him. ॥49॥
6.19.50: Likewise the others should bow to him in accordance with the tradition. Then the disciple, rising, should likewise bow to the guru, to his guru's guru, and to the disciples of his own guru as well. ॥50॥
6.19.51: To the disciple who has thus made his prostrations, of good conduct, restrained in speech, standing bowed in humility, the guru himself should give this instruction: ॥51॥
6.19.52: From today onward be devoted to the welfare of the people. Having tested a disciple for a year, accept him according to the rule. ॥52॥
6.19.53: Having abandoned faults such as passion, be devoted to meditation on Śiva. Keep company with those perfected in a true tradition, and not with others. ॥53॥
6.19.54: Never eat without first worshipping Śiva, as long as life lasts. Firmly holding to devotion to the guru, be happy, be happy. ॥54॥
6.19.55: Thus, in due order, the excellent guru, compassionate, an ocean of knowledge, should treat the disciple as his equal with a kindly mind. ॥55॥
6.19.56: Out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, lord of sages, I have told you this procedure of the yogapaṭṭa, though it is very secret. ॥56॥
6.19.57: Having said this, the six-faced Skanda, with affection and out of compassion for ascetics, began to explain to him the auspicious sequence of the rite of shaving and bathing. ॥57॥
6.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The description of the rite of the yogapaṭṭa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
6.20.1: Subrahmaṇya said: O Vāmadeva, great sage, I shall describe the procedure for shaving and bathing, by whose performance the ascetic at once attains supreme purity. ॥1॥
6.20.2: O lord of sages, once the disciple has received the rite of the yogapaṭṭa, he becomes a complete observer of vows; he should then make ready for the act of shaving. ॥2॥
6.20.3: Having bowed to the guru with special reverence and then obtained the guru's permission, he should wash his head, sip water, and, still wearing his garment, undergo the shaving. ॥3॥
6.20.4: Afterwards he should wash the cloth and the razor and other tools with clay and water; and having smeared the barber's hands with clay, he should give him clay, saying, Wash. ॥4॥
6.20.5: The tools having been set down and sprinkled with water while he utters Śiva, Śiva, and his own eyes having been closed and charged with mantra by the ring finger and thumb, ॥5॥
6.20.6: opening them with the Astra mantra, he should look at the shaving implements, the razor and the rest; then, having charged them twelve times, he should sprinkle them with the Astra mantra. ॥6॥
6.20.7: Taking the razor with the Tāra (Om), he should cut on the right side; and having himself shaved some hairs at the tips, he should have all the rest shaved. ॥7॥
6.20.8: Placing a leaf on the ground, he should cast the hair onto it, not onto the bare surface of the earth. He should also have the beard and the nails of hands and feet cut. ॥8॥
6.20.9: Gathering clay from the spot of a bilva, aśvattha, tulasī or similar plant, and having plunged twelve times into the water, going to the bank and sitting down, ॥9॥
6.20.10: placing the clay on a clean spot and dividing it into three, and again dividing each into three in the same way, he should sprinkle it and consecrate it with the Astra mantra. ॥10॥
6.20.11: Taking one portion of clay there and having it passed by the other hand, he should smear both hands twelve times and wash each one with water. ॥11॥
6.20.12: Again, taking in the hand in due order one portion for the feet and another for the face, having smeared and washed them with water, he should enter the water once more. ॥12॥
6.20.13: Dividing another portion of clay, smearing it in order twelve times on the head down to the face, and plunging again and again, ॥13॥
6.20.14: going to the bank, he should take sixteen mouthfuls of water for rinsing, sip water twice, and again restrain the breath with the praṇava sixteen times. ॥14॥
6.20.15: Again dividing another portion of clay into three, and with one of them cleansing the hips and the feet, sipping water twice, ॥15॥
6.20.16: then, restrained in speech, restraining the breath sixteen times with the praṇava, and again placing another portion on his thigh in three parts with Om, ॥16॥
6.20.17: he should sprinkle it and consecrate it seven times; then, having smeared the palms of his hands with one part three times, he should gaze upon the purifying form of the Sun. ॥17॥
6.20.18: Then, with another portion of clay, the wise and firm-minded disciple should smear both his armpits with his hands crossed over, ॥18॥
6.20.19: and likewise, devoted to his guru, taking another pure portion of clay, he should smear himself from head to feet, with his gaze fixed on the Sun. ॥19॥
6.20.20: Then, rising and taking up his staff from the ground, he should with devotion and steadfastness in knowledge remember his own guru, the giver of the mantra. ॥20॥
6.20.21: Then the disciple should devoutly remember Śiva together with Ambā — Maheśāna, Śaṅkara, the moon-crested one, lord of all sovereignty. ॥21॥
6.20.22: He should lovingly prostrate three times with all eight limbs to the guru and to Śiva, and once with five limbs; then, rising, he should offer salutation. ॥22॥
6.20.23: Entering the sacred water, plunging and emerging in its midst, and placing that clay on his shoulder, he should smear himself in the manner described before. ॥23॥
6.20.24: Gathering what remains there and going into the midst of the water, stirring it thoroughly there and smearing it on all his limbs, ॥24॥
6.20.25: uttering Om three times and remembering Śiva's lotus feet, which carry one across the ocean of worldly existence — for he always acts according to the rule — ॥25॥
6.20.26: having sprinkled himself with Om using water mixed with Virajā ash, and having wiped his body, he should then bathe thoroughly with ash. ॥26॥
6.20.27: Then, O sage, having applied the auspicious tripuṇḍra attentively by the prescribed method on all the prescribed limbs, ॥27॥
6.20.28: then, becoming pure in mind, he should perform the midday rites, bowing to Maheśvara, to the gurus, and to the sacred waters and the like. ॥28॥
6.20.29: O sage, he should worship with supreme devotion Maheśāna together with Ambikā, the giver of knowledge and protector of the three worlds. ॥29॥
6.20.30: Then that firm-minded ascetic, established in his own dharma and pure, should go out for alms among good communities of brāhmaṇas. ॥30॥
6.20.31: And there, pure in self, he should collect alms in the fivefold manner as is proper, and should avoid defiled food. ॥31॥
6.20.32: Purification, bathing, alms-seeking, and constant resort to solitude — these are the four duties of a mendicant; there is no fifth. ॥32॥
6.20.33: A gourd, a bamboo vessel, a wooden one and an earthen one — these are the four vessels of a mendicant; there is no fifth. ॥33॥
6.20.34: Betel, a metal vessel, emission of semen, white clothing, sleeping by day, and food at night — these six are forbidden to ascetics. ॥34॥
6.20.35: Those who are sākṣara (learned) yet perverse are known as rākṣasas (sākṣarā read in reverse). Therefore an ascetic should never do any contrary deed. ॥35॥
6.20.36: An ascetic should diligently perform the shaving and bathing for the sake of purity, remembering in his mind the pure supreme Brahman, Sadāśiva. ॥36॥
6.20.37: Thus, O tiger among sages, out of affection for you I have told the entire procedure of shaving and bathing. What more do you wish to hear? ॥37॥
6.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The description of the rite of shaving and bathing, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
6.21.1: Vāmadeva said: For those ascetics who are liberated there is no cremation rite; I have heard that when the body has died, that body is buried. ॥1॥
6.21.2: O Kārttikeya, my teacher, kindly explain that rite to me with great affection, for there is no one other than you in the three worlds who can expound it. ॥2॥
6.21.3: Those who, resting in the sense of complete I-ness, are freed from the cage of the body, and those who, freed from the body by the path of worship, have gone to the Supreme — ॥3॥
6.21.4: O blessed son of Śaṅkara, considering me your own disciple, please kindly tell me the particular destiny of these. ॥4॥
6.21.5: Sūta said: Hearing the sage's request, the son of Śakti, slayer of the enemies of the gods, spoke that utmost secret which Bhṛgu had heard from the Lord. ॥5॥
6.21.6: Subrahmaṇya said: O sage, this very secret was told directly to Bhṛgu, the Śiva-yogin, by the omniscient Lord, the bearer of the Pināka. ॥6॥
6.21.7: I shall tell it to you today, O brahmin; it must not be given to just anyone. It should be given only to a disciple who is tranquil and endowed with devotion to Śiva. ॥7॥
6.21.8: If there is some ascetic who, established in samādhi, gives up the body in the awareness of being Śiva, that greatly steadfast one becomes the all-full Śiva. ॥8॥
6.21.9: But whoever is unsteady in mind and does not attain samādhi — I shall tell the means for him; listen attentively. ॥9॥
6.21.10: Having heard from the guru's mouth the full knowledge of the three categories, born of the words of the Vedānta and the Āgamas, he should practise yoga, beginning with yama. ॥10॥
6.21.11: Doing that properly, the ascetic should be intent on meditation on Śiva, O sage, always, with discipline, his mind attached to the praṇava. ॥11॥
6.21.12: If, owing to weakness of the body, the ascetic lacks steadiness, then, free of desire and remembering Śiva, he should give up his worn-out body. ॥12॥
6.21.13: O sage, by the grace of Sadāśiva, impelled by Nandin, there are five renowned deities in the form of conductors (ātivāhika) of the departed. ॥13॥
6.21.14: One has the form of the identity of fire, with a body that is a mass of light; one presides over the day; one presides over the bright fortnight; ॥14॥
6.21.15: and one in the form of the northern course of the sun — these five are intent on grace. The other five are smoke, the dark night, the one presiding over the dark fortnight, ॥15॥
6.21.16: and the one in the form of the southern course — these are known as the other five deities. Now hear their function, O Vāmadeva, great sage. ॥16॥
6.21.17: Those five deities take the souls devoted to performing ritual works and go to heaven by virtue of their merit, O sage. ॥17॥
6.21.18: Having enjoyed the pleasures as described, when that merit is exhausted they again reach the human world and take birth as before. ॥18॥
6.21.19: Those first five, in turn, dividing the path into five stages beginning from the earth and taking him in the order beginning with fire, lead the ascetic to the abode of Sadāśiva — ॥19॥
6.21.20: having led him to the adorable feet of the God of gods, they stand behind him, embodiments of grace, employed in this very task. ॥20॥
6.21.21: Seeing him arrived, Sadāśiva, the God of gods — if he is dispassionate — teaches him the inner meaning of the great mantra, ॥21॥
6.21.22: and gives him a body equal to his own, and consecrating him to the leadership of the gaṇas, Śaṅkara, Lord of all, leader of all, bestows grace on him. ॥22॥
6.21.23: That body is adorned with the deer, the axe, the excellent trident and the boon-granting gesture, three-eyed, bearing the crescent moon, and wearing matted locks gleaming with the Gaṅgā. ॥23॥
6.21.24: and seated on the finest aerial car, all-pervading, granting all desires. Thus, for one whose dispassion is partial, he grants an aerial car surrounded by maidens of Rudra, ॥24॥
6.21.25: charming with the sound of dance, song, mṛdaṅga drums and other instruments, and adorned with divine garments, garlands, unguents and ornaments, ॥25॥
6.21.26: full of jars of divine nectar, filled with divine waters, shining like millions of suns, cool as millions of moons, ॥26॥
6.21.27: swift as thought and going everywhere — granting such an aerial car; and when that one, having enjoyed the pleasures, loses his curiosity for enjoyment, ॥27॥
6.21.28: the Lord, causing to descend on him the most intense Śakti, by nature extremely hard to attain, eager to burn the wilderness of bondage, radiant as the fire of dissolution, ॥28॥
6.21.29: the Supreme Lord, granting the inner meaning of the great mantra — the unwavering conviction, I am the full Śambhu, in the form of pure awareness — ॥29॥
6.21.30: and granting samādhi, along with unobstructed powers (siddhi) which are the pulsation of his own service and consist in the capacity for the functions of the sun and others, ॥30॥
6.21.31: at the end of the lifespan of the lotus-born Brahmā, the Guru of the world bestows upon him supreme liberation, free from return. ॥31॥
6.21.32: Therefore this very state is endowed with all lordship and is all-comprehensive, and is the highway to liberation — such is the conclusion of the Vedāntas. ॥32॥
6.21.33: Then, around that weak, dying ascetic who belongs to the true tradition, ascetics should stand, out of goodwill. ॥33॥
6.21.34: Then all of them there, concentrated, should impart in due order the sayings beginning with the praṇava and their purport, ॥34॥
6.21.35: and should describe them clearly and lovingly, constantly causing him to remember Śiva, the attributeless supreme Light, bowing to him until his dissolution. ॥35॥
6.21.36: Here the sequence of rites for these ascetics is stated as the same for all. For those whose bodies have not received cremation rites, no evil destiny arises. ॥36॥
6.21.37: Since they, having renounced all actions, are wholly devoted to taking refuge in Śiva, the kingdom of a king who defiles their body perishes. ॥37॥
6.21.38: The inhabitants of that village too would become greatly afflicted. For removing that fault, the procedure is stated as follows. ॥38॥
6.21.39: With a humble mind, he should at that time recite the mantra beginning with nama iriṇyāya ca and ending with nama āmīvatkebhyaḥ. ॥39॥
6.21.40: Reciting Om at the end, he should then fill up the sacred pit; then indeed, O lord of sages, that fault is pacified. ॥40॥
6.21.41: Sons and others should perform the excellent rite for the dead ascetic in proper order. Out of kindness I shall describe it, O brāhmaṇa; listen attentively. ॥41॥
6.21.42: Having worshipped the body, bathed it with pure water, and worshipped it with flowers and the like, with the Śrī Rudra and Camaka and with the Rudra-sūkta in due order, ॥42॥
6.21.43: and having placed a conch in front and sprinkled the body with its water, placing a flower on the head, he should wipe it with the Praṇava. ॥43॥
6.21.44: Removing the loincloth and other garments, he should put others on it again. Then he should smear its whole body with ash according to rule. ॥44॥
6.21.45: Having made the tripuṇḍra three lines according to rule and a tilaka with sandal paste, he should adorn the body with flowers and garlands. ॥45॥
6.21.46: On the chest, throat, head, arms, forearms and ears in order, he should adorn it with rudrākṣa garlands and ornaments, with mantras. ॥46॥
6.21.47: Having fumigated it well with incense, lifting it up and placing it on a sling, he should set the body on a beautiful chariot consisting of the five Brahma mantras. ॥47॥
6.21.48: With the five Brahma mantras beginning with Om, Sadyojāta and the rest in order, he should adorn that chariot with fragrant flowers and garlands. ॥48॥
6.21.49: With dance and music and the chanting of the Vedas by brāhmaṇas on all sides, carrying that dead body, he should go around the village keeping it to the right. ॥49॥
6.21.50: Then all those ascetics, in the east or else in the north, in a holy place near a sacred tree, ॥50॥
6.21.51: having dug a sacrificial pit to the measure of a staff, should sprinkle it with the Praṇava and the Vyāhṛtis and strew it in order, ॥51॥
6.21.52: with śamī leaves and flowers; above that, spreading darbha grass with tips to the north, he should make a seat covered with cloth, deerskin and kuśa. ॥52॥
6.21.53: Sprinkling that body with the Praṇava, the Brahma mantras and the pañcagavya, and bathing it with the Rudra-sūkta and the Praṇava, ॥53॥
6.21.54: and bathing it with conch water, he should place a flower on the head. He the performer, intent on remembering Śiva, acts in accordance with the departed one. ॥54॥
6.21.55: Then, lifting the body with Om, preceded by the svastivācana, he should set it in the pit in a yogic posture so that it faces east. ॥55॥
6.21.56: Having adorned it with scents and flowers, then with incense of guggulu, saying Viṣṇo havyam and uttering rakṣasva, he should offer it. ॥56॥
6.21.57: He should place the staff in the right hand and the water-pot in the left, with water, with the mantra Prajāpate na tvad etāny anyo. ॥57॥
6.21.58: Touching the head with the mantra Brahma jajñānaṃ prathamam, and having recited the Rudra-sūkta, he should recite while touching the space between the brows, ॥58॥
6.21.59: then with the four verses beginning Mā no mahāntam. Then he should break open the head with a coconut, and then fill the pit. ॥59॥
6.21.60: Touching the spot with the five Brahma mantras, with undivided mind he should recite: He who, preceding the gods, he who is supreme, he is Maheśvara — ॥60॥
6.21.61: having thus recited and meditated on Mahādeva together with Ambā, the remedy for saṃsāra, omniscient, dependent on none, the bestower of grace on all, ॥61॥
6.21.62: he should then make with clay a platform one cubit high and two cubits wide, and smear it with cow-dung. ॥62॥
6.21.63: And drawing a square in its middle, he should worship with sandal and unbroken rice, fragrant flowers, bilva leaves and tulasī. ॥63॥
6.21.64: Then with the Praṇava he should offer incense and lamp, milk and food-offering; having offered, circumambulated, he should bow down five times. ॥64॥
6.21.65: Having recited the Praṇava twelve times, he should then bow, and with the Praṇava offer the brahmārghya in the order of the directions and intermediate directions. ॥65॥
6.21.66: Thus the procedure for ascetics up to the tenth day has been told to you; now, O best of sages, hear the procedure of the eleventh day. ॥66॥
6.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The description of the rites for ascetics from death up to the tenth day, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥21॥
6.22.1: Subrahmaṇya said: When the eleventh day has arrived, I shall tell you, O tiger among sages, out of affection for you, the rite that has been prescribed for ascetics. ॥1॥
6.22.2: Having swept the altar, smeared it, performed the puṇyāhavācana, the declaration of the auspicious day, and sprinkled it, he should draw five diagrams in order, beginning from the west and ending in the east, ॥2॥
6.22.3: he himself, seated facing north, should make the diagrams, each conceived as a span in size, with a square in the middle, ॥3॥
6.22.4: and, in order, shaped as a dot, a triangle, a hexagon and a circle. Placing a conch in front, following the sequence stated for worship, ॥4॥
6.22.5: having restrained the breath, made the resolve, and worshipped the sovereign goddesses — the five deities mentioned earlier, who take the form of conveyors (ātivāhika) of the departed, ॥5॥
6.22.6: he should then cast away the darbha grass to the north and touch water. Beginning from the west, by the method of the sixfold seat, ॥6॥
6.22.7: he should treat the diagrams as seats, placing flowers within them as on a pedestal. Saying Om hrīṃ, he should invoke that conveying deity in the form of fire, ॥7॥
6.22.8: with the words, I invoke … namaḥ, at the end; he should contemplate this everywhere, and should reverently show to each deity the mudrās beginning with the installation mudrā. ॥8॥
6.22.9: With hrāṃ hrīṃ and so on he should perform, in order, the consecration of their limbs. He should meditate on them as holding in their hands noose, goad, and the gestures of fearlessness and boon, radiant like moonstone, ॥9॥
6.22.10: colouring all the quarters with the lustre of their red finger-rings, wearing red garments, adorned with lotus-like hands and feet, ॥10॥
6.22.11: charming with full-moon faces shining with three eyes, decorated with the crescent moon gleaming on ruby crowns, ॥11॥
6.22.12: their cheeks brushed by earrings, with full and high breasts, lovely with necklaces, armlets, bracelets and girdle-strings, ॥12॥
6.22.13: slender-waisted, broad-hipped, clothed in red divine garments, with lotus feet tinkling with ruby anklets, graceful and exceedingly charming with toe-rings and adorned hips. ॥13॥
6.22.14: What indeed cannot be accomplished by grace embodied, as by Śiva? Therefore, by grace embodied as Śakti, everything can be accomplished, as by Maheśa. ॥14॥
6.22.15: These five forms have been adopted by the very Bestower of grace to all; they are divine, accomplishing every task, intent on bestowing supreme grace. ॥15॥
6.22.16: Having thus meditated on all of them, auspicious and devoted to grace, he should offer water for washing their feet with drops of water from the conch. ॥16॥
6.22.17: He should offer water for sipping into their hands and arghya onto their heads, and with drops of conch water he should conceive the rite of their bathing. ॥17॥
6.22.18: He should offer divine red garments with upper cloths, and give priceless ornaments beginning with crowns. ॥18॥
6.22.19: He should offer fragrant sandal paste, very beautiful unbroken rice grains, and sweet-smelling, lovely flowers. ॥19॥
6.22.20: He should offer incense of supreme fragrance and a lamp with a ghee-soaked wick, saying, I offer all, beginning with the praṇava and hrīṃ ॥20॥
6.22.21: and ending with namaḥ. Then he should offer milk-rice drenched in honey, mixed with ghee and sugar, and filled out with cakes, bananas and jaggery, ॥21॥
6.22.22: filled and fragrant, on a banana leaf for each one. Uttering bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, he should perform the sprinkling and the other purifications. ॥22॥
6.22.23: Uttering Om hrīṃ, he should offer the food offering with svāhā (the wife of Fire), and saying, this drinking water, namaḥ, he should offer it with supreme love. ॥23॥
6.22.24: Then, O best of sages, he should lovingly remove the offerings, starting from the east, and having cleaned the place, he should offer mouth-rinsing water, sipping water and arghya. ॥24॥
6.22.25: Having offered betel, incense and lamp, and performed circumambulation and prostration, he should pray to them, placing his joined palms on his head: ॥25॥
6.22.26: May the auspicious Mothers, well pleased, commend this ascetic, who seeks the state of Śiva, as one to be protected at the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord. ॥26॥
6.22.27: Having thus prayed to them all and dismissed them to return as they came, he should take up their prasāda and give it to young girls, ॥27॥
6.22.28: or give it to cows, or cast it into water — never otherwise. Here itself he should perform the pārvaṇa śrāddha; never the ekoddiṣṭa śrāddha for an ascetic. ॥28॥
6.22.29: Here I declare the rule for the pārvaṇa śrāddha; listen to it, O best of sages, through which welfare will follow. ॥29॥
6.22.30: The performer, having bathed, having restrained his breath, wearing the sacred thread, composed, with the pavitra ring on his hand, saying, On this holy lunar day, ॥30॥
6.22.31: and resolving, I shall perform the pārvaṇa śrāddha, should place excellent darbha grass to the north for seats, and touch water. ॥31॥
6.22.32: Having invited four brāhmaṇas, devotees of Śiva, firm in their vows, who have been anointed with oil and have bathed, he should devoutly seat them there, ॥32॥
6.22.33: saying, May you do the favour of representing the Viśvedevas, then, you, for the Self, and also, for the Inner Self, ॥33॥
6.22.34: and, for the Supreme Self — having spoken and requested them thus, the ascetic's performer should reverently and with faith make the formal choosing of them, as is proper. ॥34॥
6.22.35: Having washed their feet and seated them facing east, having adorned them with sandal and the rest, he should feed them in front of Śiva. ॥35॥
6.22.36: Having smeared the ground here with cow-dung and spread darbha grass arranged with tips to the east, with breath restrained, resolving the offering of the piṇḍas, ॥36॥
6.22.37: resolving, I shall perform it, and having worshipped the three diagrams, then naming the Self, the Inner Self and the Supreme Self, ॥37॥
6.22.38: pronouncing each name in the dative case and then saying, this piṇḍa, and uttering, I give, he should offer the piṇḍas with his own devotion. ॥38॥
6.22.39: Then he should offer kuśa-water according to rule and procedure. Then, rising, he should perform circumambulation and prostration. ॥39॥
6.22.40: Then, having given the fee to the brāhmaṇas according to rule, he should perform the Nārāyaṇa-bali at that very place on the same day. ॥40॥
6.22.41: The rite of worshipping Viṣṇu is prescribed everywhere for the sake of protection alone. Therefore one should perform a great worship of Viṣṇu and offer rice cooked in milk (pāyasa). ॥41॥
6.22.42: Then, having invited twelve brahmins who have mastered the Vedas, and having worshipped them as Keśava and the rest with sandal-paste, flowers, unbroken rice and so on, ॥42॥
6.22.43: having given them sandals, umbrellas, garments and the like according to rule, one should please them with great devotion and with various auspicious words. ॥43॥
6.22.44: Having spread darbha grass with its tips pointing east, and having uttered bhūḥ svāhā and bhuvaḥ, bhuvaḥ svāhā, each preceded by the praṇava (Om), one should offer the rice cooked in milk as a bali-offering on the ground. ॥44॥
6.22.45: The proper procedure for the eleventh day has been described by me, O lord of sages. I shall now explain the procedure for the twelfth day; listen attentively, O twice-born one. ॥45॥
6.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named The description of the rites of the eleventh day for ascetics, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥22॥
6.23.1: Subrahmaṇya said: On the twelfth day, having risen early, bathed in the morning and performed his daily rites, he should invite Śiva's devotees, or ascetics, or brāhmaṇas dear to Śiva. ॥1॥
6.23.2: having invited them and called them together at midday, bathed and pure, he should feed them with devotion, according to rule, with various excellent and tasty foods. ॥2॥
6.23.3: In the presence of the Supreme Lord, having seated them there, restraining his breath and controlling his speech, he should worship them by the method of the five enclosures. ॥3॥
6.23.4: Having made the resolve by the method of the great saṅkalpa, saying, I shall perform here the worship of our guru, he should then touch the darbha grass. ॥4॥
6.23.5: Having washed their feet and sipped water, the performer himself, silent, should seat them on seats, facing east and adorned with ash. ॥5॥
6.23.6: There he should meditate on those eight in order beginning with Sadāśiva, and on the other twice-born too, O sage, with supreme reverence. ॥6॥
6.23.7: He should meditate on the Parameṣṭhi-guru, by his own name, with the notion that he is Śiva with Ambā; then on the guru, the parama-guru after him, and then the parāpara-guru. ॥7॥
6.23.8: Saying, this is the seat, he should arrange the seats, uttering each one's name preceded by praṇava and ending in the accusative case, ॥8॥
6.23.9: and adding, I invoke, obeisance; having invoked them, then with arghya water he offers water for the feet, water for sipping, arghya, garments, scents and unbroken rice too, ॥9॥
6.23.10: having given these and adorned them with flowers, then with fragrant flowers worshipping with the eight names beginning with praṇava, in the dative and ending with namaḥ, ॥10॥
6.23.11: and having offered incense and lamp, saying, May all the worship performed be complete, he should rise and bow. ॥11॥
6.23.12: Spreading plantain leaves as plates and purifying them with water, serving pure rice, sweet milk-rice, cakes, dal and side dishes first, ॥12॥
6.23.13: having given foods along with bananas, coconut and jaggery, he should give the plates and seats separately, announcing them in order. ॥13॥
6.23.14: Having sprinkled water around and over the food, saying, This is Viṣṇu's offering, and having had them touch it with the hand saying, Protect, he rises, ॥14॥
6.23.15: and having offered the āpośana water, he should then pray to them thus: May Sadāśiva and the others be pleased and grant boons to me. ॥15॥
6.23.16: Then, having recited ye devāḥ, he should release this water with unbroken rice; having bowed and risen, saying, May there be nectar everywhere, ॥16॥
6.23.17: having said this and gratified them, reciting from the beginning gaṇānāṃ tvā, the Vedas and so on, the Rudra and Camaka, the Rudra-sūkta and the five sūktas, ॥17॥
6.23.18: continuing the mantras until the end of the brāhmaṇas' meal, and having given water with unbroken rice, the final āpośana, and water for cleansing hands, feet and mouth, ॥18॥
6.23.19: and having had this done, seating them, after they have sipped water, comfortably on their own seats, giving pure water and then camphor and the like as prescribed, ॥19॥
6.23.20: mouth-freshener, a fee, sandals, a seat, a leaf, a fan, a plank and a bamboo staff — having given these to them, ॥20॥
6.23.21: having pleased them with circumambulations and prostrations, he should obtain their blessing; bowing again and praying for unwavering devotion to the guru, ॥21॥
6.23.22: saying, May Sadāśiva and the others, pleased, depart at their ease, having thus given them leave and duly following them as far as the door, ॥22॥
6.23.23: and being stopped by them, he should turn back and, together with the brāhmaṇas at the door, relatives, and the poor and helpless, eat and remain at ease. ॥23॥
6.23.24: Nothing will go wrong anywhere — this is true, true, again and again. One who performs this excellent worship of the guru thus every year, having enjoyed great pleasures here, will attain Śiva's world. ॥24॥
6.23.25: Sūta said: Having thus spoken to his own disciple, the excellent sage Śrī Vāmadeva, on whom he had bestowed grace, the god — great-souled, foremost of the wise, with a gladdened mind — having swiftly granted supreme grace, said further: ॥25॥
6.23.26: That which was formerly told to the lords of sages of the Naimiṣa forest by Vyāsa, lord of sages — therefore he is the first teacher, and you are the second noble one, renowned in the world. ॥26॥
6.23.27: Having heard it from your lotus-mouth, Sanatkumāra, lord of sages, full of devotion to Śiva, will tell it to Vyāsa; and he, best of Śaivas, perfect in knowledge, will tell it to Śuka. ॥27॥
6.23.28: Each one, O tiger among sages, has a group of four disciples, engaged in Vedic study and devoted to establishing dharma. ॥28॥
6.23.29: Vaiśampāyana, Paila, Jaimini and Sumantu — these four are the mighty disciples of Vyāsa. ॥29॥
6.23.30: Agastya, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu are your great-souled disciples, O Vāmadeva, great sage. ॥30॥
6.23.31: Sanaka, Sananda, then the sage Sanātana, and Sanatsujāta — these are the foremost yogins, dear to Śiva. ॥31॥
6.23.32: They are the disciples of Sanatkumāra, the best knowers of the meaning of all the Vedas. The guru, the parama-guru, then the parātpara-guru and the parameṣṭhi-guru — these are to be worshipped as the gurus of the yogin Śuka. ॥32॥
6.23.33: This knowledge of the praṇava abides in these four groups; it is the supreme source of all, and in Kāśī the cause of true liberation. ॥33॥
6.23.34: May this wondrous maṇḍala — ever the form of Paraśiva's abode, supreme, worthy of worship by the foremost ascetics whose minds are filled with inquiry into the meaning of Vedānta, and enveloped too by the great ether and the rest arranged according to the divisions of the Veda and so on — thus be a source of your satisfaction, a bringer of welfare to the worlds and a giver of prosperity. ॥34॥
6.23.35: This supreme secret, spoken by Śiva, firmly ascertained by the conclusions of Vedānta, which you have heard from me — therefore, O sage, the wisest will call it your doctrine. ॥35॥
6.23.36: Therefore the ascetic who goes to Śiva by this very path, realising, I am Śiva, becomes Śiva, for release from the distinctions beginning with Brahmā, just as these rivers go to the ocean. ॥36॥
6.23.37: Sūta said: Having thus taught this to the lord of sages, the lord of the gods, remembering the lotus feet of his parents, worshipped by all the gods, ॥37॥
6.23.38: Kumāra, the guru who bestows divine knowledge, reached the summit of Kailāsa, surrounded by peaks, resplendent and supremely wondrous. ॥38॥
6.23.39: Vāmadeva too, surrounded by his good disciples, having bowed to the peacock-rider, quickly went to the supremely wondrous Kailāsa. ॥39॥
6.23.40: Having gone to the summit of Kailāsa and come near the Lord, the sage beheld the feet of the divine Pair, which grant liberation and destroy māyā. ॥40॥
6.23.41: With devotion, having offered all his limbs in prostration and forgetting his own body, he fell down in their presence; having bowed again and again, he rose up. ॥41॥
6.23.42: Then the sage praised the Supreme Lord, together with Ambikā and with their son, with many kinds of hymns full of the essence of the Vedas and Āgamas. ॥42॥
6.23.43: Placing the lotus feet of the God and the Goddess upon his own head and obtaining their full grace, he dwelt happily right there. ॥43॥
6.23.44: You too, having thus known Maheśvara as the meaning of the Praṇava, the secret of the Vedas, the all-in-all, the Tāraka, Brahman, the giver of liberation, ॥44॥
6.23.45: remaining happily right here at the feet of Śrī Viśveśvara, attain the supreme, incomparable liberation in the form of sāyujya (union). ॥45॥
6.23.46: I shall go to the Badarī hermitage to serve the lotus feet of my guru. May I again have good conversation with you. ॥46॥
6.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The account of the line of disciples, Vyāsa and the others, preceded by the description of the rites of the twelfth day, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥23॥
